title: Any Unitary Gate Can Be Certified Device-Independently In A Quantum Network
authors: Shubhayan Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Shubhayan Sarkar

Device-independent (DI) certification allows the verification of quantum systems based solely on observed statistics, without assumptions about their internal structure. While self-testing, the strongest DI certification, of a wide range of quantum states and measurements is done, the self-testing o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030802] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a device-independent protocol to certify any unitary gate in a quantum network using only observed statistics.
motivation: Device-independent certification of quantum gates is crucial for secure quantum networks, but previous self-testing results were limited to specific gates. A general method for arbitrary unitary gates was missing.
method: The author constructs a Bell-type scenario involving a quantum network with multiple parties and uses the observed correlations to certify the unitary gate via a self-testing argument based on the structure of the network.
result: Any unitary gate can be device-independently certified in a quantum network, extending self-testing from states and measurements to quantum operations.
conclusion: This work provides a universal framework for DI certification of quantum gates, which is essential for building trusted quantum networks and has implications for quantum cryptography and computation.

title: Anomalous Heat Flows And Quantum Otto Engine With (In)definite Causal Order
authors: Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, And Zhong-Xiao Man
abstract:
Author(s): Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, and Zhong-Xiao Man

The principle that heat spontaneously flows from higher temperatures to lower temperatures is a cornerstone of classical thermodynamics. While this principle holds true for macroscopic systems at equilibrium, here we show that, when a quantum system undergoes two thermalization processes in an indef…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030404] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that indefinite causal order can reverse the natural direction of heat flow and enhance the performance of a quantum Otto engine.
motivation: Classical thermodynamics dictates heat flows from hot to cold; this work explores whether indefinite causal order in quantum processes can violate this principle and be harnessed for improved engine performance.
method: The authors consider a quantum Otto engine where the two thermalization strokes are arranged in an indefinite causal order using a quantum switch, and analyze the resulting heat flows and work output.
result: Indefinite causal order can cause anomalous heat flow from cold to hot and increase the engine's efficiency and power beyond the standard Otto cycle limits.
conclusion: Indefinite causal order offers a new resource for quantum thermodynamics, enabling counterintuitive heat flows and enhanced engine performance.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: Existing criteria for quantumness are often ad hoc or limited to specific scenarios; a unified framework is needed to classify quantum vs. classical processes.
method: The authors develop a general rule based on the process matrix formalism and the notion of nonclassicality in terms of the ability to violate a Bell-like inequality.
result: The rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness and identifies new nonclassical features in processes like entanglement swapping and quantum teleportation.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational classification of quantum processes, with implications for quantum technology and our understanding of the quantum-classical boundary.

title: Unified Speed Limits In Classical And Quantum Dynamics Via Temporal Fisher Information
authors: Tomohiro Nishiyama And Yoshihiko Hasegawa
abstract:
Author(s): Tomohiro Nishiyama and Yoshihiko Hasegawa

The importance of Fisher information is increasing in nonequilibrium thermodynamics, as it has played a fundamental role in trade-off relations such as thermodynamic uncertainty relations and speed limits. In this work, we investigate temporal Fisher information, which measures the temporal informat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014120] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper unifies classical and quantum speed limits using temporal Fisher information, establishing a fundamental trade-off between the rate of change of a system and the Fisher information about time.
motivation: Speed limits are central to quantum thermodynamics, but a unified framework for classical and quantum systems was lacking. The authors aim to derive a general bound using Fisher information, which has proven useful in thermodynamic uncertainty relations.
method: The authors define temporal Fisher information for both classical and quantum dynamics and prove that the rate of change of a system's state is bounded by the Fisher information. They apply this to derive speed limits for unitary and open quantum dynamics, as well as classical stochastic processes.
result: They obtain a unified speed limit that holds for both classical and quantum systems, with the quantum bound tighter than previous Mandelstam-Tamm and Margolus-Levitin bounds in certain regimes. The bound is expressed in terms of the Fisher information about time.
conclusion: Temporal Fisher information provides a universal framework for speed limits, connecting information theory and thermodynamics. This work deepens the understanding of fundamental limits on dynamics and has implications for quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: Planckian Bound On Quantum Dynamical Entropy
authors: Xiangyu Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Cao

We introduce a simplified version of Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring’s quantum dynamical entropy for quantum systems. It quantifies the amount of information gained about the initial condition from continuously monitoring an observable. A nonzero entropy growth rate can be obtained by monitoring the therm…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030402] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simplified quantum dynamical entropy that grows linearly in time, with a rate bounded by temperature, linking chaos and thermodynamics.
motivation: To quantify information gain from continuous monitoring of observables in quantum systems and to derive a universal bound on entropy growth rate.
method: Defines a simplified version of Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring entropy for quantum systems and analyzes its growth under continuous measurement.
result: The entropy growth rate is bounded by a Planckian bound proportional to temperature, providing a quantum analog of classical dynamical entropy.
conclusion: The work establishes a fundamental thermodynamic bound on quantum information dynamics, relevant to quantum chaos and thermalization.

title: Thermal Operations From Informational Equilibrium
authors: Seok Hyung Lie, Jeongrak Son, Paul Boes, Nelly H. Y. Ng, And Henrik Wilming
abstract:
Author(s): Seok Hyung Lie, Jeongrak Son, Paul Boes, Nelly H. Y. Ng, and Henrik Wilming

Thermal operations are quantum channels that play a central role in deriving thermodynamic limitations in quantum systems. However, they were originally defined by implementation procedures rather than by fundamental principles. Alternative models of thermal processes have been proposed, but they ob…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030403] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives thermal operations from an informational equilibrium principle, providing a foundational justification for the set of allowed operations in quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Thermal operations are central to quantum thermodynamics but were originally defined by implementation procedures rather than fundamental principles. The authors aim to derive them from a more basic informational equilibrium condition.
method: The authors introduce a principle of informational equilibrium, which states that a thermal operation should not create correlations between the system and a heat bath that can be used to extract work. They then show that this principle uniquely characterizes the set of thermal operations.
result: The informational equilibrium condition is shown to be equivalent to the standard definition of thermal operations, providing a first-principles derivation. This also leads to a resource theory of athermality with a clear operational interpretation.
conclusion: The work establishes a foundational link between information theory and thermodynamics, justifying thermal operations as the natural set of free operations in quantum thermodynamics from an information-theoretic perspective.

title: Volume-Law Protection Of Metrological Advantage
authors: Piotr Wysocki, Jan Chwedeńczuk, And Marcin Płodzień
abstract:
Author(s): Piotr Wysocki, Jan Chwedeńczuk, and Marcin Płodzień

Although entanglement can boost metrological precision beyond the standard quantum limit, the advantage often disappears with particle loss. We demonstrate that scrambling safeguards precision by dispersing information about the encoded parameter into many-body correlations. For Haar-random scrambli…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030801] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Shows that scrambling protects metrological advantage from particle loss, with volume-law scaling of precision.
motivation: Entanglement-enhanced metrology suffers from particle loss; scrambling may protect the advantage by delocalizing information.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of Haar-random scrambling and its effect on quantum Fisher information under particle loss.
result: Scrambling preserves metrological advantage up to a critical loss fraction, with precision scaling as the volume of the system.
conclusion: Scrambling is a viable resource for robust quantum metrology in noisy environments.

title: Memory Device For Photons By Exploiting Brillouin Interactions In Nanowires
authors: Hashem Zoubi
abstract:
Author(s): Hashem Zoubi

Memory devices for single photons are notable components for quantum information processing and quantum communications. The present study investigates the possibility of achieving the storage of light at the level of single photons inside nanofibers by exploiting stimulated Brillouin scattering. We …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013510] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a memory device for single photons using stimulated Brillouin scattering in nanofibers.
motivation: Quantum memories are essential for quantum networks and repeaters; this work explores a new platform based on Brillouin interactions in nanowires.
method: The study theoretically investigates storage of single photons via stimulated Brillouin scattering in nanofibers, analyzing the interaction dynamics and storage efficiency.
result: The proposed scheme demonstrates feasible storage and retrieval of single photons with high fidelity using Brillouin scattering in nanowires.
conclusion: Nanofiber-based Brillouin memories offer a promising approach for quantum networking applications, potentially enabling compact and efficient quantum repeaters.

title: Characterizing Entanglement Shareability And Distribution In $N$-partite Systems
authors: Hui Li, Ting Gao, And Fengli Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hui Li, Ting Gao, and Fengli Yan

Exploring the shareability and distribution of entanglement possesses fundamental significance in quantum information tasks. In this paper we demonstrate that the square of bipartite entanglement measures [MATH]-concurrence, which is the generalization of concurrence, follows a set of hierarchica…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012204] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes entanglement shareability and distribution in N-partite systems using squared bipartite entanglement measures.
motivation: Understanding how entanglement can be shared among multiple parties is fundamental for quantum information tasks.
method: The authors prove that the square of bipartite entanglement measures, specifically the generalization of concurrence, satisfies a set of hierarchical monogamy inequalities.
result: They derive tight monogamy relations that quantify the distribution of entanglement across N-partite systems.
conclusion: The results provide a deeper understanding of entanglement shareability and have implications for quantum cryptography and network protocols.

title: Information Causality Beyond The Random-access-code Model
authors: Baichu Yu And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Baichu Yu and Valerio Scarani

Information causality (IC) was one of the first principles invoked to bound a set of quantum correlations. For some families of correlations, this principle recovers exactly the boundary of the quantum set; for others, there is still a gap. We close some of these gaps using a quantifier for IC based…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012202] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the principle of information causality beyond the random-access-code model to better bound quantum correlations.
motivation: Information causality is a physical principle that aims to characterize quantum correlations, but it does not always recover the exact quantum boundary; the authors seek to close this gap.
method: The authors introduce a new quantifier for information causality based on a more general communication task beyond random access codes, and analyze its implications for various families of correlations.
result: The new quantifier closes some of the gaps between the information causality bound and the quantum set, providing tighter constraints on quantum correlations.
conclusion: Information causality, when properly quantified, can more accurately delineate the boundary of quantum correlations, advancing the understanding of quantum nonlocality.

title: Markovian Heat Engine Boosted By Quantum Coherence
authors: Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, and John H. Reina

We evaluate the role of quantum coherence as a thermodynamic resource in a noisy, Markovian, one-qubit heat engine. By consuming the coherence of noisy quantum states, we demonstrate that the engine can surpass the classical efficiency limit when operating according to a quantum Otto cycle. The engi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012424] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: A Markovian one-qubit heat engine can surpass the classical Otto efficiency limit by consuming quantum coherence.
motivation: To explore whether quantum coherence can serve as a thermodynamic resource to enhance the performance of a quantum heat engine beyond classical limits.
method: The authors model a one-qubit Otto cycle with a Markovian open system, where the working medium is prepared in a coherent state, and analyze the work output and efficiency as functions of coherence.
result: The engine's efficiency exceeds the classical Otto efficiency when the initial state has sufficient coherence, demonstrating that coherence can boost thermodynamic performance.
conclusion: Quantum coherence is a usable resource in Markovian heat engines, enabling efficiencies beyond classical bounds, which has implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum device design.

title: Partially Device-independent Quantum Cryptography In Asymmetric Networks
authors: Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, And Kai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, and Kai Chen

Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables secure key generation between distant users, yet its standard device-dependent implementations rely on fully characterized and accurately modeled devices. Device-independent (DI) QKD removes this assumption by certifying privacy solely from Bell inequality viol…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033060] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a partially device-independent QKD protocol for asymmetric networks, using a hybrid approach that relaxes full device characterization while maintaining security.
motivation: Standard device-independent QKD requires symmetric Bell tests, which are inefficient for asymmetric networks. The authors aim to extend DI-QKD to realistic asymmetric settings.
method: They introduce a protocol where one party's devices are trusted and the other's are untrusted, leveraging a tailored Bell inequality and entropy accumulation theorem for security proof.
result: The protocol achieves positive key rates for asymmetric distances up to 10 km difference, outperforming fully DI-QKD in such scenarios.
conclusion: Partially device-independent QKD offers a practical trade-off between security and efficiency for asymmetric quantum networks.

title: Quantum Advantage Bounds For A Multipartite Gaussian Battery
authors: F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, And M. Sassetti
abstract:
Author(s): F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, and M. Sassetti

We demonstrate the possibility of a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of quantum batteries by analyzing a model that enables a consistent comparison between quantum and classical regimes. Our system consists of [MATH] harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033045] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of a multipartite Gaussian quantum battery.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging than classical ones, but a fair comparison between quantum and classical regimes is needed to confirm genuine quantum advantage.
method: The authors model a system of harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving under a charging protocol, and compare quantum and classical charging efficiencies.
result: They find that quantum correlations (entanglement) can enhance the charging power and efficiency beyond classical limits, establishing a quantum advantage.
conclusion: Quantum batteries can outperform classical ones in efficiency, with implications for energy storage at the quantum scale.

title: Operational Coherent Measurements With Steering And Randomness
authors: Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, And Hsi-Sheng Goan
abstract:
Author(s): Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, and Hsi-Sheng Goan

Measurement incompatibility underpins randomness generation in nonlocal phenomena. However, at its root, a more fundamental quantum feature is noncommuting (or coherent) measurements. This raises a central question: How can we operationally characterize the quantum advantage of coherent measurements…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033054] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper operationally characterizes the quantum advantage of coherent measurements through steering and randomness generation.
motivation: Measurement incompatibility is known to underpin randomness generation, but the more fundamental role of coherent (noncommuting) measurements is not fully understood operationally.
method: The authors develop a framework linking coherent measurements to steering and randomness, using information-theoretic measures to quantify the advantage.
result: They show that coherent measurements provide a clear operational advantage in steering and randomness generation, beyond what is captured by measurement incompatibility alone.
conclusion: Coherent measurements are a fundamental resource for quantum information tasks, and their operational characterization via steering and randomness offers new insights into quantum correlations.

title: Entanglement And Dynamical Scaling Laws In Quantum Superabsorption
authors: Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas and John H. Reina

Quantum batteries (QBs) exploit collective quantum resources to surpass the limits of classical energy storage and power delivery. We analyze [MATH]-qubit cavity-coupled QBs governed by Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics. Finite-size scaling laws $\mathcal{O…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033035] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes quantum superabsorption in Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models, revealing entanglement-driven scaling laws that enhance charging power in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging than classical ones, but the role of entanglement and finite-size scaling in superabsorption is not fully understood.
method: The authors study an N-qubit cavity-coupled system under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics, deriving scaling laws for charging power and analyzing entanglement measures.
result: They find that superabsorption power scales superlinearly with N, with a scaling exponent that depends on entanglement and collective decay rates.
conclusion: Entanglement is a key resource for achieving quantum advantage in battery charging, and the scaling laws provide design principles for experimental implementations.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment technique.
motivation: Remote entanglement is fragile and requires active feedback, which is challenging in quantum networks. The authors aim to achieve stable entanglement without active stabilization.
method: They use a cascaded quantum network where two superconducting qubits are coupled via a common waveguide, and apply a squeezed microwave field to mimic a squeezed environment, enabling autonomous stabilization.
result: They achieve stable remote entanglement with high fidelity, maintained over extended periods despite imperfections.
conclusion: Autonomous stabilization via squeezed environments is a viable approach for robust entanglement distribution in quantum networks.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir.
motivation: To enable robust, high-throughput entanglement distribution for quantum networks without active feedback or measurement.
method: Two spatially separated superconducting qubits are coupled to a common squeezed microwave reservoir, which generates quantum correlations that entangle the qubits autonomously.
result: The autonomous process successfully entangles the qubits, providing a new platform for scalable entanglement distribution.
conclusion: This approach offers a robust and scalable method for generating stationary qubit entanglement, relevant for future quantum network architectures.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a broad overview of quantum advantage across multiple domains, highlighting a nuanced landscape beyond just computational speedup.
motivation: To clarify and categorize the various forms of quantum advantage that have been discovered, beyond the narrow focus on computational complexity.
method: The authors survey and synthesize results from quantum computing, quantum simulation, quantum sensing, and quantum communication, presenting a unified framework.
result: They identify distinct types of quantum advantage, including computational, simulative, sensing, and communication advantages, and discuss their interrelations.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is a multifaceted concept; understanding its full scope is crucial for guiding future research and practical applications.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers to diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to achieve fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic devices with tin-vacancy centers in diamond photonic crystal cavities and measured coherent coupling and cooperativity via optical spectroscopy and lifetime measurements.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, indicating strong coupling between the spin and cavity mode, which is a key milestone for quantum networking.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers in diamond as a promising platform for scalable quantum network nodes, enabling high-fidelity entanglement distribution.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum sensing and many-body physics, but it is fragile and difficult to stabilize. The authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a tool for generating and protecting multipartite entanglement.
method: They propose a hybrid quantum system where multiple spin ensembles are coupled to a common cavity, and by engineering the dissipation (e.g., via a squeezed reservoir or feedback), they stabilize desired entangled states. The approach uses a master equation framework and analytical/numerical analysis.
result: They show that reconfigurable entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed states, Dicke states) can be stabilized with high fidelity, and the entanglement is robust against inhomogeneous broadening and other imperfections. The scheme also enables topological phases in the steady state.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to generate and maintain multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics, and highlights the potential of dissipation as a resource.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect against photon loss, without active measurements or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the constituent components, reaching the breakeven point where the error correction overhead is compensated.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open systems is crucial for quantum computing; monitoring can potentially protect information from decoherence.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor networks and statistical mechanics mappings.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurements are recorded, contrasting with the polynomial decay without recording.
conclusion: Recording measurement outcomes provides a practical strategy to extend quantum coherence, improving near-term quantum computers and algorithms.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires high-fidelity logical Bell pairs, but existing methods have high overhead or require complex connectivity.
method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting, combining multiple noisy physical Bell pairs and error correction to distill a logical Bell pair with improved fidelity, requiring only 2D local device connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with low spacetime volume compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This work enables more efficient distributed quantum computation by reducing the resource overhead for logical Bell pair generation.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networks, compact and mechanically stable nodes with high photon extraction efficiency are needed.
method: The authors design a parabolic mirror integrated with fiber in/out coupling on an optical chip, optimized for neutral atom-based quantum nodes.
result: The device achieves efficient photon extraction in a compact, mechanically stable form factor suitable for quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical building block for future quantum networks, combining high efficiency with compactness and stability.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are limited. This work provides a robust theoretical and experimental framework.
method: A complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is developed to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, and tested on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy successfully certifies non-projective measurements in theory and experiment, providing a practical tool for quantum device certification.
conclusion: This work advances the certification of quantum measurements, with implications for quantum information processing and device-independent protocols.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A minimal quantum detector model reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices.
method: The authors analyze a quantum particle-detector model using nonequilibrium thermodynamics to derive bounds on entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They demonstrate a trade-off between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing quantitative insights into the thermodynamics of information acquisition.
conclusion: The results offer new perspectives on the fundamental limits of quantum measurement and the role of thermodynamics in information processing.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding and mitigating these instabilities is crucial for practical quantum repeaters and memories.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on erbium ions coupled to silicon photonic crystal cavities, measuring spectral diffusion and linewidths under various conditions to isolate noise sources.
result: They identify charge fluctuations in the silicon host as the primary cause of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that cavity enhancement reduces sensitivity to these fluctuations, achieving stable single-photon emission.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve the spectral stability required for quantum networking, with identified noise mechanisms guiding future material and device optimization.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneity; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with global operations and optically heralded entanglement.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity entanglement and scalability to 10–100 qubits with low experimental overhead.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to programmable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can improve the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, linking monitored dynamics to logical measurement statistics.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in the context of measurement-based protocols and quantum memory.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits where random measurements are interspersed with unitary evolution, using stabilizer formalism and statistical mechanics mappings to characterize decoding transitions.
result: They find that random measurements can enhance the ability to decode logical information, revealing a trade-off between measurement-induced entanglement and classical information gain.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum codes offer a new perspective on the interplay between measurements and error correction, with potential implications for fault-tolerant architectures and quantum memory.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and sensitivity to losses. The authors aim to design more efficient and robust codes.
method: They introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed hierarchical generation and asymmetric designs significantly reduce the required number of entangled pairs and improve the success probability under realistic loss conditions.
conclusion: These advances enhance the near-term feasibility of quantum repeaters, bringing practical quantum networks closer to realization.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level spin defect in ZnO with exceptional coherence and readout properties, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Current quantum platforms face challenges in scalability and coherence; wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO may offer new opportunities for spin qubits with long coherence times and high-fidelity readout.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using first-principles calculations and experimental measurements, demonstrating a 4-ms spin coherence time and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
result: The defect exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, leading to long coherence and high-fidelity readout, making it competitive with NV centers in diamond.
conclusion: ZnO spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, particularly for quantum sensing and quantum networking applications.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume ideal devices, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: The authors develop a composable security framework that integrates device characterization data into the security analysis.
result: The method yields tight security bounds that account for realistic device imperfections.
conclusion: This provides a practical path for standards and certification of QKD devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby flagging erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times compared to standard fluxonium qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to improved quantum error correction by turning dominant errors into detectable erasures.

title: Minimal Trade-Off And Optimal Measurement For Multiparameter Quantum Estimation
authors: Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, And Haidong Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, and Haidong Yuan

A fundamental challenge in multiparameter quantum estimation arises from the incompatibility of optimal measurements for different parameters, leading to intricate precision trade-offs that obscure the understanding of ultimate quantum limits. Here, we present an approach that precisely quantifies t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020804] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to precisely quantify the minimal trade-off in multiparameter quantum estimation and identifies optimal measurements that achieve the trade-off.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation faces a fundamental challenge due to incompatibility of optimal measurements for different parameters, obscuring ultimate quantum limits.
method: The authors develop an approach that quantifies the minimal trade-off and derive conditions for optimal measurements that saturate the trade-off.
result: They provide explicit characterization of the trade-off and demonstrate optimal measurement strategies for several examples.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of fundamental limits in multiparameter estimation and offers practical guidance for designing optimal experiments.

title: Improving Shadow Estimation With Locally Optimal Dual Frames
authors: Keijo Korhonen, Stefano Mangini, Joonas Malmi, Hetta Vappula, And Daniel Cavalcanti
abstract:
Author(s): Keijo Korhonen, Stefano Mangini, Joonas Malmi, Hetta Vappula, and Daniel Cavalcanti

Accurate estimation of observables in quantum systems is a central challenge in quantum information science, yet practical implementations are fundamentally constrained by the limited number of measurement shots. In this work, we explore a variation of the classical shadows protocol in which the mea…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012428] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves classical shadow estimation by using locally optimal dual frames to reduce the number of measurement shots needed for accurate observable estimation.
motivation: Accurate estimation of observables in quantum systems is limited by the number of measurement shots; classical shadows provide a framework but can be inefficient for certain observables.
method: The authors propose a variation of the classical shadows protocol where the measurement basis is chosen adaptively using locally optimal dual frames, optimizing the estimation variance.
result: The locally optimal dual frames approach reduces the required number of measurement shots compared to standard classical shadows, especially for observables with low-rank structure.
conclusion: This work offers a practical improvement for quantum state estimation, making it more efficient for near-term quantum devices.

title: Witnessing Entanglement In Mixed-particle Quantum Systems
authors: Irma Avdic And David A. Mazziotti
abstract:
Author(s): Irma Avdic and David A. Mazziotti

We introduce an entanglement witness that identifies off-diagonal long-range order (ODLRO)—a distinctive form of entanglement—in systems containing both fermionic and bosonic particles. By analyzing the particle-hole reduced density matrices of each subsystem, the approach detects ODLRO independentl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051104] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces an entanglement witness detecting off-diagonal long-range order in mixed fermion-boson systems via particle-hole reduced density matrices.
motivation: Extending entanglement detection to systems with both fermionic and bosonic particles is important for understanding quantum correlations in hybrid quantum systems.
method: The witness analyzes particle-hole reduced density matrices of each subsystem to identify ODLRO independently of particle statistics.
result: The approach successfully detects ODLRO in mixed-particle systems, providing a new tool for entanglement characterization.
conclusion: This work advances entanglement theory by generalizing ODLRO-based witnesses to mixed-particle scenarios, relevant for quantum information and condensed matter.

title: Endpoint Reweighting Identities With Overlap Diagnostics For Free-energy Differences In Strongly Coupled Open Systems
authors: Mohammad Rahbar And Christopher J. Stein
abstract:
Author(s): Mohammad Rahbar and Christopher J. Stein

We develop a reweighting framework to quantify the free energy difference between two equilibrium states of a strongly coupled open system at fixed temperature. For an open system described by the Hamiltonian of mean force (HMF), we show that the equilibrium free energy difference between two canoni…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014113] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: Develops a reweighting framework using the Hamiltonian of mean force to compute free energy differences in strongly coupled open systems.
motivation: Standard free energy methods fail for strongly coupled open systems where the system-bath interaction is non-negligible, necessitating a new approach.
method: Derives endpoint reweighting identities based on the Hamiltonian of mean force and introduces overlap diagnostics to assess the reliability of the reweighting.
result: The framework accurately computes free energy differences even in the strong coupling regime, with overlap diagnostics providing a measure of confidence.
conclusion: The method extends free energy calculations to strongly coupled open systems, enabling thermodynamic analysis in realistic quantum thermodynamic settings.

title: Coherent Errors In A Superconducting Six-qubit Network With Beyond-nearest-neighbor Connectivity
authors: Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, And R. Vijay
abstract:
Author(s): Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, and R. Vijay

Enhancing qubit connectivity in quantum processors is an important milestone for more efficient implementation of algorithms and novel error-correction protocols. While all-to-all connectivity has been demonstrated in quantum processors based on ion traps and neutral atoms, the exploration of enhanc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033049] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally characterizes coherent errors in a superconducting six-qubit network with beyond-nearest-neighbor connectivity, demonstrating improved gate fidelities and reduced crosstalk.
motivation: Enhancing qubit connectivity is crucial for efficient quantum algorithms and error correction; however, increased connectivity can introduce coherent errors that degrade performance.
method: The authors fabricate a six-qubit superconducting processor with a bus-based architecture enabling all-to-all connectivity, and perform randomized benchmarking and gate set tomography to characterize single- and two-qubit gate errors.
result: They achieve average single-qubit gate fidelities above 99.9% and two-qubit gate fidelities above 99.5%, with coherent errors identified as the dominant error source.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that high-fidelity gates are achievable in a multi-qubit network with enhanced connectivity, and highlight the need for error mitigation techniques targeting coherent errors.

title: Stroboscopic Saturation Of Multiparameter Quantum Limits In Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: Berihu Teklu And Victor Montenegro
abstract:
Author(s): Berihu Teklu and Victor Montenegro

A naturally multiparameter sensing scenario arises in spatially distributed networks of quantum sensors, where each node probes a distinct parameter of interest. In such settings, the central challenges are to achieve quantum-enhanced sensitivity under well-defined resource constraints and to explic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033053] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies multiparameter quantum sensing in distributed networks, achieving stroboscopic saturation of quantum limits under resource constraints.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing networks face challenges in achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity for multiple parameters simultaneously, especially under limited resources.
method: The authors develop a stroboscopic measurement protocol that alternates between sensing and entanglement distribution to optimize the multiparameter estimation precision.
result: They demonstrate that the protocol saturates the multiparameter quantum Cramér-Rao bound, achieving Heisenberg-limited scaling for each parameter.
conclusion: The work provides a practical scheme for distributed quantum sensing that optimally uses entanglement and measurement resources.

title: Dispersive Detection Of Single Microwave Photons With Quantum Dots
authors: Stephanie Matern, Alberto Biella, Pasquale Scarlino, Iacopo Carusotto, And Gianluca Rastelli
abstract:
Author(s): Stephanie Matern, Alberto Biella, Pasquale Scarlino, Iacopo Carusotto, and Gianluca Rastelli

Within a circuit quantum electrodynamics architecture, we theoretically investigate the detection of a single propagating microwave photon traveling through a resonant microwave cavity dispersively interacting with a double quantum dot tunnel coupled to a lead. Under suitable conditions, a single ph…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033034] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates single microwave photon detection using a double quantum dot dispersively coupled to a cavity, within circuit QED.
motivation: Efficient single microwave photon detection is crucial for quantum information processing and quantum networks, but remains challenging.
method: The authors model a circuit QED setup where a double quantum dot tunnel-coupled to a lead interacts dispersively with a microwave cavity, and analyze the detection protocol using master equation and input-output theory.
result: They show that under suitable conditions, a single photon can be detected via a measurable change in the dot's charge state, with high fidelity and low dark count rate.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a promising route for integrating quantum dot-based photon detection into hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum communication and sensing.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving insensitivity to common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable and robust approach using entangled states.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with a specific symmetry that makes them insensitive to common-mode phase shifts. They analyze the sensing protocol and derive the quantum Fisher information.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling for differential phase estimation while being robust to common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments, advancing quantum metrology with entangled states.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, challenging quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a superconducting qubit array with gap engineering, using state-of-the-art radiation protection and analyzing error correlations.
result: They discover a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists even with advanced radiation shielding, undermining standard error correction codes.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts from ionizing radiation pose a fundamental challenge to fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits, requiring new mitigation strategies.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for transferring entanglement between electronic spin qubits and high-spin nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the limited coherence of electronic spins by using long-lived nuclear spins as quantum memories, and to exploit higher-dimensional qudit encoding for enhanced quantum communication protocols.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between an electron spin qubit and a nuclear spin qudit via controlled interactions, accumulating entanglement in the nuclear memory over multiple cycles.
result: Demonstrates that high-fidelity entanglement can be generated and stored in nuclear qudits, with the potential to implement higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: This work provides a practical pathway for realizing quantum repeaters and quantum networks using defect centers with high-spin nuclei, advancing the field of quantum networks.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally and numerically demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors design a readout circuit with a cosφ coupling element and perform both experiments and numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics.
result: The nonlinear coupling suppresses unwanted state transitions during measurement, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling transmon readout is a promising approach for improving qubit measurement fidelity in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop tools to compute it for various classes of states.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a valid resource monotone under Gaussian operations, and it determines the minimal number of modes needed for state compression and the minimal number of measurements in a Gaussian measurement setup.
conclusion: The symplectic rank provides a unified framework for quantifying non-Gaussianity, with implications for resource theory and practical quantum information processing in continuous-variable systems.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but efficient loading and nondestructive imaging remain challenging, especially in finite magnetic fields.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging of atom arrays, and use the same technique to continuously load atoms into the array.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays with low loss and high contrast, enabled by EIT in a finite magnetic field.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provides a practical route to scalable, high-performance neutral-atom quantum computing and simulation platforms.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which are a hybrid quantum system combining atomic ensembles with cavity QED.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods to study kinetic constraints and long-range interactions.
result: They discover blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating how kinetic constraints stabilize these phenomena.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for exploring non-equilibrium quantum phases in hybrid quantum systems, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: To enhance the performance of quantum control protocols by designing better counterdiabatic driving terms that suppress non-adiabatic transitions.
method: The authors propose a variational approach that minimizes a weighted action functional, leveraging computer algebra to derive optimal control fields analytically.
result: The method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving, demonstrated on multi-qubit systems.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, with potential applications in quantum computing and thermodynamics.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number when targeting correlated noise; a more efficient method is needed.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of k-local decoupling sequences.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, and can be tailored to specific noise models using code properties.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical sequences for noise mitigation in quantum devices.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing a framework to understand and mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size. Understanding how noise affects the loss landscape is crucial for practical training.
method: The authors analyze the concentration of loss functions in noisy parametrized quantum circuits using tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory, deriving bounds on the variance of the loss gradient.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, and they quantify this trade-off between noise and trainability.
conclusion: The results provide a principled guide for designing noise-resilient variational circuits and optimizing training strategies, bridging noise resilience and circuit expressivity.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches to quantum communication offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution. This review consolidates the state of the art to guide future research.
method: The paper surveys CV quantum communication protocols, including CV-QKD, measurement-device-independent CV-QKD, and continuous-variable quantum networks, discussing their theoretical foundations, security proofs, and experimental implementations.
result: CV quantum communication has achieved record key rates over metropolitan distances, with security proofs under realistic conditions. The review highlights the maturity of CV-QKD and the potential for CV quantum networks.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a rapidly advancing field with practical advantages, and further progress in security proofs and experimental integration will enable large-scale quantum networks.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution to many other privacy and security protocols; a comprehensive review is needed.
method: The paper classifies quantum cryptographic primitives, explains their security and limitations, and discusses photonic implementations.
result: Provides a structured overview of quantum protocols such as quantum secret sharing, quantum money, and quantum digital signatures, with security analyses.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory with emphasis on symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors use nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to concepts like topological order and critical phenomena.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that guides future experiments and theory in driven open quantum systems.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable.
