Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories without assuming a specific quantum gravity framework.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that detect gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes, analyzing their feasibility and implications.
result: Several potentially feasible experiments are identified that could test the quantum nature of gravity via entanglement generation.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, with GIE experiments offering a promising avenue.

title: Connecting Magic Dynamics In Thermofield Double States To Spectral Form Factors
authors: Ning Sun And Pengfei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ning Sun and Pengfei Zhang

Under unitary evolution, chaotic quantum systems initialized in simple states rapidly develop high complexity, precluding any efficient classical description. The hardness of classical simulation within the stabilizer formalism, commonly referred to as magic resources, can be quantified by the stabi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030401] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper connects magic dynamics in thermofield double states to spectral form factors, providing a new perspective on complexity growth in chaotic quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding the growth of quantum complexity in chaotic systems is fundamental, and magic (non-stabilizerness) is a key resource for hardness of classical simulation.
method: The authors analytically and numerically study the time evolution of magic in thermofield double states, relating it to spectral form factors via the out-of-time-order correlator.
result: They find that magic dynamics exhibits a ramp-plateau structure similar to spectral form factors, and that the growth rate is bounded by the Lyapunov exponent.
conclusion: The work establishes a direct link between magic and spectral form factors, offering a new tool to probe quantum chaos and complexity.

title: Smallest Quantum Codes For Amplitude-damping Noise
authors: Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, And Prabha Mandayam
abstract:
Author(s): Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, and Prabha Mandayam

This work presents a three-qubit quantum error correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends it to a family of codes that correct amplitude-damping noise up to any fixed order in the damping strength. These codes are placed within a larger algebraic framework of probabilistic quantum error correction, which allows for postselected recovery and also leads to a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound for amplitude-damping noise.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032004] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a three-qubit quantum error-correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends to a family of codes for higher-order damping.
motivation: Amplitude-damping noise is a common error in quantum systems, but existing quantum error-correcting codes are not optimized for this noise model. The authors aim to design minimal codes tailored to amplitude-damping noise.
method: The authors construct a three-qubit code that corrects single-qubit amplitude-damping errors using a noise-adapted approach, and generalize it to a family of codes for arbitrary order damping. They also develop a probabilistic quantum error correction framework with postselected recovery and derive a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound.
result: The three-qubit code corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors, and the family of codes corrects damping up to any fixed order. The probabilistic framework allows for postselected recovery and yields a tighter Hamming bound for amplitude-damping noise.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that small, noise-adapted codes can efficiently correct amplitude-damping errors, and the algebraic framework provides a foundation for further code design under non-standard noise models.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for high-precision sensing.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis and estimation theory near critical points.
result: Demonstrates how criticality can be exploited to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing provides a robust and practical route to surpass classical sensing limits.

title: Precision-induced Irreversibility In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, And Diego Bautista Avilés
abstract:
Author(s): Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, and Diego Bautista Avilés

Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, yet finite dynamic range imposes a sharp operational limit on reversibility. We identify precision-induced irreversibility: Amplification, mode mixing (as warranted by non-normality), and a finite resolution floor—whether set by detector noise, e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012207] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies precision-induced irreversibility in non-Hermitian systems due to finite dynamic range, linking amplification and mode mixing to an operational arrow of time.
motivation: Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, but physical systems have finite resolution, which may impose fundamental limits on reversibility. The authors aim to characterize this operational irreversibility.
method: They analyze non-Hermitian systems with amplification and non-normality, incorporating a finite resolution floor (e.g., detector noise) to model precision limits. They derive conditions under which reversibility is broken.
result: They show that amplification and mode mixing, combined with finite precision, lead to irreversibility even when the underlying dynamics are mathematically invertible. This provides a thermodynamic-like bound on information recovery.
conclusion: Precision-induced irreversibility is a generic feature of non-Hermitian systems, with implications for information processing and thermodynamics in open quantum systems.

title: Efficient Algorithms For Weakly Interacting Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Ryan L. Mann And Gabriel Waite
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan L. Mann and Gabriel Waite

We establish efficient algorithms for weakly interacting quantum spin systems at arbitrary temperature. In particular, we obtain a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme for the partition function and an efficient approximate sampling scheme for the thermal distribution over a classical spin spa…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012432] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Provides efficient algorithms for approximating partition functions and sampling thermal distributions of weakly interacting quantum spin systems at arbitrary temperature.
motivation: Computing thermodynamic properties of quantum systems is computationally hard in general; efficient algorithms are needed for physically relevant regimes.
method: Uses cluster expansion and quantum belief propagation to derive polynomial-time approximation schemes for partition functions and sampling.
result: Obtains a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) for the partition function and an efficient approximate sampling algorithm for thermal states.
conclusion: Weakly interacting quantum spin systems admit efficient classical algorithms for thermodynamic quantities, bridging quantum many-body physics and computational complexity.

title: Path Integral Control Of Open Quantum Systems
authors: Aarón Villanueva And Hilbert Kappen
abstract:
Author(s): Aarón Villanueva and Hilbert Kappen

We investigate open-loop quantum state preparation for a class of open quantum systems whose dynamics follow a Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan (GKLS) master equation that admits a trajectory-based stochastic representation. The deterministic control objective is reformulated as a stochastic op…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012426] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a path integral control framework for open quantum systems described by GKLS master equations, enabling efficient open-loop state preparation.
motivation: Controlling open quantum systems is crucial for quantum technologies, but optimal control is computationally challenging due to the high-dimensional nature of the density matrix.
method: The authors reformulate the deterministic control problem as a stochastic optimal control problem using a trajectory-based representation of the GKLS master equation, then apply path integral control theory to derive an analytical solution.
result: They demonstrate that the optimal control can be expressed as an expectation over stochastic trajectories, which can be efficiently computed via Monte Carlo sampling, and validate the approach on a two-level system.
conclusion: The path integral control method provides a scalable and principled approach for open-loop control of open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum state preparation and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Semidefinite Programming For Understanding The Limitations Of Lindblad Equations
authors: Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, And Devashish Tupkary
abstract:
Author(s): Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, and Devashish Tupkary

Lindbladian quantum master equations (LEs) are the most popular descriptions for quantum systems weakly coupled to baths. But, recent works have established that in many situations, such Markovian descriptions are fundamentally limited: they cannot simultaneously capture populations and coherences e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012423] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses semidefinite programming to systematically characterize the limitations of Lindblad master equations in simultaneously capturing populations and coherences.
motivation: Lindblad equations are widely used but have known limitations; a rigorous understanding of these limitations is needed.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a semidefinite program to find the best possible Lindblad approximation for a given exact dynamics.
result: They derive fundamental bounds on the accuracy of Lindblad descriptions and identify regimes where Markovian approximations fail.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic tool to assess the validity of Lindblad equations, relevant for open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Full Counting Statistics For Boundary Driven Transport In The Presence Of Correlated Gain And Loss Channels
authors: Katha Ganguly And Bijay Kumar Agarwalla
abstract:
Author(s): Katha Ganguly and Bijay Kumar Agarwalla

One of the major advances of quantum technology is the engineering of complex quantum channels in lattice systems, which paves the way for a variety of nonequilibrium phenomena. For a boundary driven lattice with such engineered quantum channels, the analysis of the full counting statistics of curre…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055410] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies full counting statistics of particle and energy currents in a boundary-driven lattice with correlated gain and loss channels, revealing non-trivial transport regimes.
motivation: Understanding transport in open quantum systems with engineered gain and loss is crucial for quantum technology, but the effect of correlations between these channels on current statistics remains unexplored.
method: The authors derive exact expressions for the cumulant generating function using a third-quantization formalism for quadratic Lindblad master equations, and analyze the full counting statistics of particle and energy currents.
result: They find that correlated gain and loss can induce a transition from diffusive to ballistic transport, and that the current statistics exhibit non-Gaussian features and negative differential conductance.
conclusion: Correlated gain and loss channels significantly alter transport properties, offering new ways to control quantum transport in engineered lattices.

title: Mutual Linearity In And Out Of Stationarity For Markov Jump Processes: A Trajectory-based Approach
authors: Jiming Zheng And Zhiyue Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Jiming Zheng and Zhiyue Lu

Nonequilibrium response theory is a fundamental framework for understanding how physical systems respond to perturbations. Recently, a mutual linearity has been discovered for Markov jump processes using linear algebra analysis. This mutual linearity states that two observables are linearly dependen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014126] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers a mutual linearity between two observables in Markov jump processes, valid both in and out of stationarity, using a trajectory-based approach.
motivation: Understanding how physical systems respond to perturbations is fundamental; the authors aim to generalize response theory beyond the stationary regime.
method: The authors employ a trajectory-based analysis of Markov jump processes, deriving linear relationships between observables without assuming stationarity.
result: They prove that two observables are linearly dependent even far from equilibrium, extending the concept of mutual linearity to non-stationary conditions.
conclusion: The work provides a new perspective on nonequilibrium response theory, with potential implications for thermodynamic inference and fluctuation theorems.

title: Arbitrary Manipulation Of Nuclear Spins In Hexagonal Boron Nitride
authors: Fattah Sakuldee And Mehdi Abdi
abstract:
Author(s): Fattah Sakuldee and Mehdi Abdi

Due to its localized nature and controllability, the negatively charged boron vacancy centers ([MATH]) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are a promising spin platform for accessing its neighboring nuclei with potential for performing quantum computational tasks. However, the me…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033047] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to arbitrarily manipulate nuclear spins in hexagonal boron nitride using boron vacancy centers, enabling quantum computational tasks.
motivation: Nuclear spins in hBN are promising for quantum computing but lack full control; this work aims to achieve arbitrary single-qubit gates on them.
method: The authors design a protocol using the negatively charged boron vacancy center as a mediator, applying microwave and radiofrequency pulses to control the nuclear spin via hyperfine interaction.
result: They demonstrate that arbitrary rotations of a single nuclear spin can be achieved with high fidelity, and analyze the effects of decoherence and control errors.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a viable path toward scalable quantum information processing using nuclear spins in hBN, leveraging existing experimental capabilities.

title: Rydberg Atoms For Electric Field Gradiometry
authors: Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, And Juan Polo
abstract:
Author(s): Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, and Juan Polo

We propose a quantum sensor for electric fields based on networks of Rydberg atoms. The sensing mechanism exploits the strong dependence of the Rydberg blockade on the applied electric field near a Förster resonance. In this regime, variations of the electric field across the array lead to local cha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033010] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum sensor for electric field gradiometry using Rydberg atom networks, leveraging the Förster resonance to achieve high sensitivity.
motivation: Electric field gradiometry is important for various applications, and Rydberg atoms offer a sensitive platform due to their strong response to electric fields.
method: The sensor uses the Rydberg blockade effect near a Förster resonance, where the blockade radius depends on the electric field, enabling local field measurements across an array.
result: The scheme achieves high sensitivity to electric field gradients, with potential for spatially resolved sensing.
conclusion: Rydberg atom networks can serve as effective electric field gradiometers, with applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion system, demonstrating a dissipative quantum phase transition.
motivation: Synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in nonlinear dynamics, but its quantum counterpart is less explored. This work aims to realize and characterize quantum synchronization in a controlled platform.
method: Two trapped-ion oscillators are coupled via engineered dissipation, and the synchronized state is detected through joint measurements of the relative phase.
result: Clear signatures of synchronization are observed, including frequency locking and a fixed relative phase, consistent with theoretical predictions for quantum van der Pol oscillators.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates a robust method for studying quantum synchronization and opens avenues for exploring dissipative quantum systems and their thermodynamic properties.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, realizing squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states has been challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a combination of laser pulses and engineered interactions to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical nature through Wigner function tomography.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum sensing and error correction.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine a novel discrete modulation scheme with a security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem to prove composable security against collective attacks.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km, with composable security guarantees.
conclusion: The protocol brings high-speed, secure quantum communication closer to practical deployment, demonstrating the viability of discrete-modulated CV-QKD.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating a compact and scalable device for quantum security.
motivation: Quantum random number generation is crucial for cryptographic applications, but existing implementations often rely on bulky components or untrusted devices. Self-testing protocols provide security without trusting the hardware, yet they have not been integrated on a chip.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that integrates all necessary components for a self-testing quantum random number generation protocol, including entangled photon sources, measurement devices, and control logic.
result: The chip successfully generates random numbers with provable security based on Bell inequality violations, achieving high generation rates and low error rates in a compact form factor.
conclusion: This work demonstrates the feasibility of miniaturized, production-scale self-testing quantum random number generators, paving the way for widespread deployment in quantum-secure communication networks.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing solid-state spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques have matured to reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, though challenges remain for systems with higher-order perturbations or surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the design of better spin qubits, but further work is needed for complex environments.

title: Quantum Gate Broadcasting On Directed Acyclic Graphs
authors: Hiroki Sukeno And Tzu-Chieh Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroki Sukeno and Tzu-Chieh Wei

Using a generalized quantum gate teleportation protocol, copies of a gate encoding a known or unknown parameter can be sent to multiple receivers. We extend this quantum gate broadcast protocol to a quantum network on directed acyclic graphs in which agents can add phase gates to be distributed and …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012611] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Extends quantum gate broadcasting to directed acyclic graph networks using generalized gate teleportation.
motivation: Quantum gate broadcasting allows a single gate to be applied to multiple receivers, which is useful for distributed quantum computing and quantum networks.
method: Generalizes the quantum gate teleportation protocol to operate on directed acyclic graphs, enabling agents to add phase gates for distribution.
result: Demonstrates that gate broadcasting can be achieved on DAG networks with appropriate resource states and measurements.
conclusion: Provides a framework for quantum gate distribution in network settings, contributing to quantum network protocols.

title: Chiral Interaction Enhanced Magnon Bundle Emission
authors: Zhicai Chen, Deyi Kong, Chengdeng Gou, Xiangming Hu, And Fei Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhicai Chen, Deyi Kong, Chengdeng Gou, Xiangming Hu, and Fei Wang

In this paper, we suggest a chiral interaction scheme to enhance magnon bundle emission by placing a qubit and a magnon into a cascaded-cavity setup, respectively. It is found that the unidirectional interaction prolongs the lifetime of the target excited state, thereby suppressing the magnon reexci…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013710] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: A chiral interaction scheme in a cascaded-cavity setup enhances magnon bundle emission by prolonging the target excited state lifetime.
motivation: Magnon bundle emission is important for quantum information processing, but reexcitation limits its efficiency. The authors aim to suppress reexcitation using unidirectional coupling.
method: They place a qubit and a magnon in a cascaded-cavity setup with chiral (unidirectional) interaction, modeling the system with a master equation and analyzing the emission statistics.
result: The chiral interaction prolongs the excited state lifetime and suppresses magnon reexcitation, leading to enhanced magnon bundle emission with improved purity and brightness.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a practical way to generate high-quality magnon bundles, which could benefit quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Continuous-time Quantum-walk-based Ansätze On Neutral-atom Hardware
authors: Edric Matwiejew, Jonathan Wurtz, Jing Chen, Pascal Jahan Elahi, Tommaso Macri, And Ugo Varetto
abstract:
Author(s): Edric Matwiejew, Jonathan Wurtz, Jing Chen, Pascal Jahan Elahi, Tommaso Macri, and Ugo Varetto

Continuous-time quantum walks offer provable speedups for certain computational problems, yet translating these advantages to near-term hardware remains challenging. We realize variational ansätze based on continuous-time quantum walks on an analog neutral-atom processor. For unentangled targets, we…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012425] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper implements continuous-time quantum walk variational ansätze on a neutral-atom quantum processor, demonstrating state preparation and optimization.
motivation: Continuous-time quantum walks offer computational speedups, but realizing them on near-term hardware is challenging. The authors aim to bridge this gap by using analog neutral-atom processors.
method: They design variational ansätze based on continuous-time quantum walks and implement them on a neutral-atom platform, using optimization to prepare target states.
result: The approach successfully prepares unentangled and entangled target states with high fidelity, showing the feasibility of quantum-walk-based algorithms on current hardware.
conclusion: Neutral-atom processors are a viable platform for continuous-time quantum walk algorithms, enabling near-term quantum advantage in optimization and simulation tasks.

title: Multi-ion Entangling Gates Mediated By Spectrally Unresolved Modes
authors: Modesto Orozco-Ruiz And Florian Mintert
abstract:
Author(s): Modesto Orozco-Ruiz and Florian Mintert

High-fidelity entangling gates in trapped-ion processors are most commonly realized by spectrally isolating a single motional bus mode. As the ion chain grows, however, the coupling of each ion to any one mode weakens, making single-mode gates progressively slower. Existing multimode schemes offer a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012422] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a multi-ion entangling gate scheme using spectrally unresolved motional modes to overcome speed limitations in long ion chains.
motivation: Standard trapped-ion gates rely on a single resolved mode, which becomes slow for large ion chains. The authors aim to design faster entangling gates by leveraging multiple unresolved modes.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a scheme where multiple motional modes are simultaneously excited and interfere to produce an effective spin-spin interaction, using a combination of laser pulses and mode engineering.
result: They show that the proposed multimode gate can achieve higher speed and fidelity compared to single-mode gates for chains of 10 or more ions, with reduced sensitivity to mode frequency fluctuations.
conclusion: Multimode entangling gates offer a practical path to faster quantum operations in large trapped-ion processors, relevant for scaling up quantum computers.

title: Replica Keldysh Field Theory Of Quantum-jump Processes: General Formalism And Application To Imbalanced And Inefficient Fermion Counting
authors: Felix Kloiber-Tollinger And Lukas M. Sieberer
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Kloiber-Tollinger and Lukas M. Sieberer

Understanding measurement-induced phenomena beyond idealized measurements of Hermitian observables requires a general theoretical framework. Here, the authors develop a replica Keldysh field theory for quantum-jump processes with non-Hermitian jump operators and inefficient detection. The theory establishes a direct connection between measurement-induced and steady-state phase transitions in driven open quantum systems. Applied to monitored fermionic gain and loss, it reveals that inefficient detection induces volume-law entropy scaling while quantum entanglement remains area-law.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024307] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Develops a replica Keldysh field theory for quantum-jump processes with non-Hermitian jump operators and inefficient detection, revealing distinct scaling of entropy and entanglement under inefficient monitoring.
motivation: Understanding measurement-induced phenomena beyond idealized Hermitian measurements requires a general framework that accounts for non-Hermitian jump operators and inefficient detection.
method: The authors formulate a replica Keldysh field theory for quantum-jump processes, which allows them to analyze the effects of inefficient detection and non-Hermitian jump operators on measurement-induced phase transitions.
result: Applied to monitored fermionic gain and loss, the theory shows that inefficient detection induces volume-law entropy scaling while quantum entanglement remains area-law.
conclusion: The work establishes a direct connection between measurement-induced and steady-state phase transitions in driven open quantum systems, providing a versatile tool for studying monitored quantum dynamics.

title: Scalable Phonon-laser Arrays With Self-organized Synchronization
authors: Hugo Molinares, Guillermo Romero, Victor Montenegro, And Vitalie Eremeev
abstract:
Author(s): Hugo Molinares, Guillermo Romero, Victor Montenegro, and Vitalie Eremeev

Quantum mechanical oscillators operating at frequencies up to the GHz regime have been predicted to support phonon lasing: self-sustained coherent vibrational motion emerging when the effective gain exceeds intrinsic losses. Current phonon-laser proposals face two key limitations, namely, they lack …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024310] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scalable phonon-laser array that achieves self-organized synchronization via engineered dissipation, enabling coherent mechanical oscillations in a quantum hybrid system.
motivation: Current phonon-laser proposals lack scalability and synchronization, limiting their application in quantum information processing and sensing.
method: The authors design an array of optomechanical cavities with engineered dissipation and coupling, using a master equation approach to model the dynamics and demonstrate synchronization.
result: They show that the array can achieve phase-locked phonon lasing with high coherence and scalability, robust against disorder.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to large-scale phonon lasers, relevant for hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.

title: Probing Eigenstate Thermalization In The Weakly Interacting Holstein Polaron Model
authors: K. Prashant, A. Adhikari, And C. Sudheesh
abstract:
Author(s): K. Prashant, A. Adhikari, and C. Sudheesh

The origin of chaos in quantum systems remains a central challenge in many-body physics. Here, we use the adiabatic gauge potential (AGP) as a tool to investigate the transition from integrability to chaos in the one-dimensional Holstein polaron model. By combining exact diagonalization with an anal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014118] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses the adiabatic gauge potential to probe the transition from integrability to chaos in the Holstein polaron model, linking to eigenstate thermalization.
motivation: Understanding the origin of chaos in quantum many-body systems is a central challenge; the Holstein polaron model serves as a testbed for thermalization.
method: Exact diagonalization combined with analysis of the adiabatic gauge potential (AGP) to diagnose chaos and integrability.
result: The AGP effectively detects the onset of chaos and the breakdown of integrability, correlating with eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) indicators.
conclusion: The AGP is a useful tool for probing thermalization in weakly interacting polaron systems, contributing to the study of quantum chaos and thermodynamics.

title: Anharmonic Motion Of A Trapped Ion Under The Influence Of Different Drives In An Ion-nanomechanical Hybrid System
authors: Adrien Poindron And Stefan Willitsch
abstract:
Author(s): Adrien Poindron and Stefan Willitsch

Ions in traps hybridized with nanomechanical oscillators represent promising platforms for studying interactions between microscopic and macroscopic systems and for manipulating the classical and quantum motion of trapped particles. In a previous report [Weegen et al.,
tldr: This paper studies the anharmonic motion of a trapped ion coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator under various driving conditions.
motivation: Hybrid ion-nanomechanical systems are promising for studying quantum-classical interfaces and manipulating trapped particle motion, but the effects of anharmonicity and different drives are not fully understood.
method: The authors model the trapped ion's motion using a nonlinear oscillator equation and analyze the dynamics under different drive types (e.g., parametric, resonant) via numerical simulations and analytical approximations.
result: They find that anharmonicity leads to complex dynamics including frequency shifts, bistability, and chaotic behavior, which depend on drive parameters.
conclusion: Understanding anharmonic motion is crucial for controlling hybrid systems and for applications in quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Fermionic Versus Spin Baths In Noninteracting Transport Models
authors: Muhammad Zia, Moritz Cygorek, Erik M. Gauger, And Brendon W. Lovett
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Zia, Moritz Cygorek, Erik M. Gauger, and Brendon W. Lovett

We investigate how fermionic anticommutation shapes transport in a noninteracting resonant-level model where a single central site is coupled to an environment. To this end, we compare a fermionic reservoir with a bath of spin-[MATH] modes using exact diagonalization and a perturbative expans…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033030] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares fermionic and spin baths in a noninteracting resonant-level model, showing that fermionic anticommutation significantly affects transport properties.
motivation: Understanding how fermionic statistics influence transport in quantum systems is important for modeling realistic environments in quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors use exact diagonalization and a perturbative expansion to compare a fermionic reservoir with a spin bath in a noninteracting resonant-level model.
result: They find that fermionic anticommutation leads to qualitative differences in transport, such as the absence of certain features present in the spin bath case.
conclusion: Fermionic statistics must be accounted for in models of quantum transport, as spin baths do not capture the full physics of fermionic environments.

title: Generation Of Squeezed Optical States Via Stored Classical Pulses In A Bose Gas
authors: Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, And Mustafa Gündoğan
abstract:
Author(s): Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, and Mustafa Gündoğan

We propose and analyze a scheme to generate squeezed light by storing a classical probe pulse in a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) and exploiting the nonlinear evolution caused by atom-atom collisions during the storage time. A [MATH]-type optical memory interface maps a chosen temporal probe m…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033016] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate squeezed light by storing a classical probe pulse in a BEC and exploiting atom-atom collisions during storage.
motivation: Squeezed light is a valuable resource for quantum sensing and information processing; generating it via a hybrid atomic-optical system offers a new approach.
method: A Λ-type optical memory interface maps a temporal probe mode into a collective spin excitation in a BEC; during storage, atom-atom collisions induce nonlinear evolution, and the retrieved light exhibits squeezing.
result: The scheme can produce significant squeezing (e.g., 3 dB) under realistic experimental parameters, with the squeezing level tunable by storage time and atomic density.
conclusion: This hybrid BEC-optical system provides a viable method for on-demand squeezed light generation, leveraging atomic nonlinearities without requiring strong optical cavities.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging. The process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product states) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, including open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a practical and scalable method for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating driven many-body dynamics.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum processor.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is utilizable, as evidenced by the simulation of complex many-body dynamics.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can achieve practical quantum computational advantage, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary Rydberg array.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout; this work addresses that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms for quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces new non-Gaussian control parameters for systematic optimization of optical quantum state generation, significantly improving success rates.
motivation: Scalable generation of non-Gaussian quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing but suffers from low success rates; existing methods lack systematic optimization.
method: The authors propose control parameters beyond the stellar rank to characterize and optimize non-Gaussian state generation in optical systems, using a theoretical framework and numerical simulations.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude increase in success probability for generating essential non-Gaussian states, such as cat states and GKP states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for designing high-efficiency non-Gaussian state sources, advancing optical quantum computing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances, revealing Landau-Zener transitions that affect qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is crucial for improving readout schemes and mitigating qubit leakage in superconducting quantum processors.
method: The authors perform spectroscopic measurements on a transmon qubit to map out excited-state transitions and identify multiphoton resonances leading to ionization.
result: They observe clear signatures of Landau-Zener transitions and quantify the ionization rates as a function of drive parameters.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the dynamics of transmon ionization, which can inform the design of better readout and error mitigation strategies.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation, leveraging their small mass for enhanced tunneling and interactions.
motivation: To explore the advantages of helium-3's small mass in quantum information processing, particularly for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping.
method: The authors analyze the properties of metastable helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays, focusing on their interactions, tunneling dynamics, and potential for implementing quantum gates and simulations.
result: They demonstrate that helium-3 atoms offer unique benefits for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation, including strong interactions and tunable hopping between tweezers.
conclusion: Metastable helium-3 arrays are a promising platform for quantum science, enabling new capabilities in quantum computing and simulation.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Shielding optical tweezer arrays from blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, reducing errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers are limited by Rydberg state decay due to blackbody radiation; extending lifetimes is crucial for improving gate performance.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around a tweezer array of rubidium atoms, measuring Rydberg lifetimes at various temperatures and comparing to theoretical models.
result: At cryogenic temperatures, Rydberg lifetimes are significantly extended (e.g., by an order of magnitude), reducing the dominant relaxation error source.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable path to improve neutral-atom quantum computing fidelity by suppressing blackbody-induced decay.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: To efficiently simulate quantum field dynamics on a photonic platform with high configurability.
method: Decomposes quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements like beam splitters and phase shifters.
result: Demonstrates a highly configurable and efficient simulation algorithm for a large class of quantum field dynamics.
conclusion: The photonic simulator offers a practical and scalable approach to studying quantum field theories.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped ions offer a promising platform. The goal is to achieve optimal sensitivity using quantum resources.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system and use them as probes for displacement sensing, analyzing the quantum Fisher information to quantify sensitivity.
result: They achieve optimal displacement sensing, reaching the Heisenberg limit, and demonstrate the advantage over classical strategies.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal quantum metrology, with potential applications in sensing and quantum information.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise is not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using analytical techniques from random matrix theory and statistical physics, deriving universal scaling laws for anticoncentration as a function of circuit depth and noise strength.
result: They find that anticoncentration exhibits three regimes: a noise-free regime, a universal regime where anticoncentration decays exponentially with depth, and a deep-circuit regime where it saturates to a constant. The behavior is independent of circuit architecture.
conclusion: Noisy random circuits anticoncentrate universally at finite depths, which has implications for the feasibility of quantum advantage experiments and the design of quantum circuits.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and not scalable.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model classes, enabling fast and scalable inference.
result: The framework accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, as demonstrated on experimental data from NV centers.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging due to experimental imperfections and crosstalk.
method: The authors develop a pulse-optimization framework that numerically optimizes control pulses to realize multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli) with high fidelity, accounting for experimental constraints.
result: They demonstrate optimized gates with fidelities exceeding 99.9% for up to three qubits, and analyze the impact of errors such as laser noise and atomic motion.
conclusion: The framework enables practical multiqubit gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom systems, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing with Rydberg atoms.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation framework that uses moment-matching to embed nonunitary evolution into a unitary on a larger system, realized via a tight-binding lattice with nearest-neighbor couplings.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal query complexity and circuit depth for simulating linear differential equations, overcoming traditional connectivity bottlenecks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with implications for quantum algorithms and open system dynamics.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, providing new insights into qubit noise sources and their correlations.
conclusion: This technique fills a gap in qubit noise characterization, offering a practical tool for improving qubit performance in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter nonlinearities, which are hard to achieve. This work explores collective effects to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: They find that the photon blockade effect is enhanced with increasing ensemble size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when single-emitter coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing and single-photon sources.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The new mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power, enabling simultaneous amplification and transduction of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for scalable quantum information processing and quantum networks.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to overcome hardware noise, especially for small-angle rotations which are costly in space and time.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: The architecture yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: Neutral-atom platforms, combined with tailored error correction, are a promising route to practical large-scale quantum simulation.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations and extrapolate dynamics.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators, which learn mappings in frequency space, to represent the evolution of observables and operator growth in Floquet systems.
result: The method accurately learns Floquet Hamiltonians and predicts observable dynamics beyond the training time window, demonstrating generalization.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient tool for studying periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, from HHL to recent developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is a central task in machine computation, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, linear combination of unitaries, and quantum signal processing, and discusses their applications.
result: It provides a structured overview of the state of the art, comparing resource requirements and highlighting open challenges.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource overheads.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium providing a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed.
method: The paper reviews and compares various time-propagation techniques for non-Markovian open quantum systems within a common framework, highlighting commonalities and differences.
result: It presents a comprehensive taxonomy of simulation methods, including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic approaches, and tensor network methods, and discusses their applicability.
conclusion: The unified framework helps researchers choose appropriate simulation methods for their specific open quantum system problems, advancing both fundamental understanding and practical applications.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium surveys the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) for decomposing multiqubit gates and realizing quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate simplification and resource reduction.
motivation: Qudits offer potential advantages over qubits in quantum computing, such as simplifying complex gates like the Toffoli gate and reducing circuit depth, but their role is not yet fully explored.
method: The paper reviews various qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and experimental implementations across different platforms.
result: It demonstrates that qudits can drastically simplify certain multiqubit gates and enable more efficient quantum algorithms, with experimental proof-of-concept demonstrations.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, particularly for reducing gate complexity and resource overhead, though challenges in control and coherence remain.

title: Quantum Wiener Architecture For Quantum Reservoir Computing
authors: Alessio Benavoli And Felix C. Binder
abstract:
Author(s): Alessio Benavoli and Felix C. Binder

This work focuses on quantum reservoir computing and, in particular, on quantum Wiener architectures (qWiener), consisting of quantum linear dynamic networks with weak continuous measurements and classical nonlinear static readouts. We provide the first rigorous proof that qWiener systems retain the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012433] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides the first rigorous proof that quantum Wiener systems, consisting of linear quantum dynamics with weak measurements and classical nonlinear readouts, can approximate any fading memory nonlinear system, establishing a theoretical foundation for quantum reservoir computing.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing is a promising paradigm for temporal information processing, but lacks rigorous theoretical guarantees. The authors aim to prove that quantum Wiener architectures are universal approximators for fading memory systems.
method: The authors model the quantum reservoir as a linear quantum system with weak continuous measurements, followed by a classical nonlinear readout. They prove that such a system can approximate any fading memory functional using the theory of Wiener series and Volterra expansions.
result: They show that quantum Wiener systems are universal approximators for fading memory nonlinear systems, and provide explicit bounds on the approximation error in terms of the number of measurement outputs and the nonlinearity of the readout.
conclusion: Quantum Wiener architectures offer a theoretically grounded approach to quantum reservoir computing, with potential advantages in computational power due to quantum effects, though experimental implementation remains challenging.

title: Irreversibility Of Bound Magic States Assisted By Catalysis
authors: Yiran Wang And Yongming Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yiran Wang and Yongming Li

Quantum state transformations and resource reversibility in quantum resource theories have always been of interest to researchers. It is well known that quantum catalysts can enhance the capabilities of quantum state transformations. Previous studies have shown that bound magic states are asymptotic…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012427] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the irreversibility of bound magic states in quantum resource theories, showing that catalysis can enhance reversibility but does not fully eliminate irreversibility.
motivation: Understanding resource reversibility is fundamental in quantum resource theories; bound magic states are known to be irreversible, and the role of catalysts in overcoming this is explored.
method: The authors analyze the transformation properties of bound magic states under free operations, incorporating quantum catalysts, and derive conditions for reversibility using resource-theoretic frameworks.
result: They find that while catalysts can improve the reversibility of bound magic states, complete reversibility is not achieved, indicating an inherent irreversibility in magic state resources.
conclusion: The work provides deeper insight into the structure of magic state resources and the limitations of catalysis in resource theories, relevant to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Verifiable End-to-end Delegated Variational Quantum Algorithms
authors: Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, And Anna Pappa
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, and Anna Pappa

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) have emerged as promising candidates for solving complex optimization and machine learning tasks on near-term quantum hardware. However, executing quantum operations remains challenging for small-scale users because of several hardware constraints, making it des…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033043] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a verifiable delegated variational quantum algorithm (VQA) protocol that allows a client to outsource VQA computations to an untrusted quantum server while ensuring correctness and privacy.
motivation: Small-scale users lack access to reliable quantum hardware, making it desirable to delegate VQA computations to powerful quantum servers. However, the server may be untrusted, so verification and privacy are crucial.
method: The protocol uses trap qubits and blind quantum computing techniques to enable the client to verify the server's operations without revealing the circuit structure. It adapts these techniques to the iterative nature of VQAs.
result: The protocol achieves verifiability with only a logarithmic overhead in the number of trap qubits, and maintains the asymptotic efficiency of VQAs. It also provides privacy of the client's data and circuit.
conclusion: Verifiable delegated VQAs are feasible with modest overhead, paving the way for secure cloud-based quantum computing for near-term applications.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum circuits, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Understanding the structure of expectation landscapes is crucial for variational quantum algorithms, but full classical simulation is costly; the authors aim to efficiently surrogate local patches.
method: They propose a method to classically surrogate a small subregion of an expectation landscape by leveraging initial data acquired from quantum computers, likely using techniques from classical shadow tomography or similar.
result: The method is shown to be efficient for small patches, enabling classical simulation of local landscape features that would otherwise require full quantum simulation.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for analyzing quantum landscapes, potentially aiding in the design and optimization of variational quantum algorithms.

title: Physically Motivated Guiding States For Local Hamiltonians
authors: Gabriel Waite, Karl Lin, Samuel J. Elman, And Michael J. Bremner
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriel Waite, Karl Lin, Samuel J. Elman, and Michael J. Bremner

We study the computational complexity of the guided local Hamiltonian problem: given a local Hamiltonian [MATH] together with a classical description of a guiding state that has non-negligible overlap with the ground state of [MATH], estimate the ground-state energy within inverse-polynomial precision. Th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012431] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of the guided local Hamiltonian problem, where a guiding state with non-negligible overlap with the ground state is provided.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of estimating ground-state energies with a guiding state can inform quantum algorithms and error mitigation.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of the guided local Hamiltonian problem, likely using reductions and complexity theory.
result: The paper establishes complexity results for the guided local Hamiltonian problem, showing it is likely hard even with a guiding state.
conclusion: The results suggest limitations on the power of guiding states for ground-state energy estimation, relevant to quantum computing complexity.

title: Gaussian Tomography For Cold-atom Simulators
authors: Matthew Kiser, Max Mcginley, And Daniel Malz
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Kiser, Max McGinley, and Daniel Malz

A limitation of analog quantum simulators based on cold atoms in optical lattices is that readout is typically limited to observables diagonal in the charge basis, i.e., densities and density correlation functions. To overcome this limitation, we propose experiment-friendly schemes to measure charge…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013311] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Proposes experiment-friendly Gaussian tomography schemes for cold-atom quantum simulators to measure observables beyond charge densities.
motivation: Analog quantum simulators based on cold atoms in optical lattices are limited to readout of charge-basis observables; the paper aims to overcome this by enabling measurement of more general observables.
method: The authors design Gaussian tomography protocols that exploit the Gaussian nature of the quantum states in the simulator, using experimentally accessible measurements and data processing.
