result: The proposed schemes allow efficient reconstruction of Gaussian states and estimation of observables such as correlations and entanglement witnesses.
conclusion: Gaussian tomography provides a practical tool to extend the readout capabilities of cold-atom simulators, enhancing their utility for quantum simulation.

title: Randomly Measured Quantum Particles And Thermal Noise
authors: Victor Gurarie
abstract:
Author(s): Victor Gurarie

We consider the motion of a quantum particle whose position is measured in random places at random moments in time. We contrast this motion with the motion of a quantum particle in a potential which varies randomly in space and in time, which could also be thought of as (possibly thermal) noise. We …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012205] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the motion of a quantum particle under random position measurements and compares it to motion in a random potential, linking to thermal noise.
motivation: To understand the effect of random measurements on quantum dynamics and contrast it with classical thermal noise.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a quantum particle subjected to random position measurements at random times, compared with a particle in a spatiotemporally random potential.
result: The random measurement process leads to diffusive behavior similar to that induced by thermal noise, but with distinct features.
conclusion: Random measurements can mimic thermal noise in quantum systems, offering insights into the interplay between measurement and thermodynamics.

title: Weakly Fault-tolerant Computation In A Quantum Error-detecting Code
authors: Christopher Gerhard And Todd A. Brun
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Gerhard and Todd A. Brun

Many current quantum error-correcting codes that achieve full fault tolerance suffer from having low ratios of logical to physical qubits and significant overhead. This makes them difficult to implement on current noisy intermediate-scale quantum computers and results in the inability to perform qua…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012429] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a weakly fault-tolerant computation scheme within a quantum error-detecting code, aiming to reduce overhead for near-term quantum devices.
motivation: Full fault-tolerant quantum error correction requires high overhead, making it impractical for current NISQ devices. The authors aim to develop a lighter-weight approach that still provides some protection against errors.
method: They design a computation protocol using a quantum error-detecting code (likely a [[4,2,2]] code or similar) that detects errors without full correction, and analyze its fault tolerance properties under a weak fault-tolerance model.
result: The scheme achieves a lower logical error rate than unprotected computation for certain noise regimes, though it does not achieve full fault tolerance. Overhead is significantly reduced compared to full error correction.
conclusion: Weakly fault-tolerant computation in error-detecting codes offers a practical intermediate step for near-term quantum computing, trading off some error suppression for reduced resource requirements.

title: Simple Analytical Model Describing The Collective Nonlinear Response Of An Ensemble Of Two-level Emitters Weakly Coupled To A Waveguide
authors: Max Schemmer, Martin Cordier, Lucas Pache, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, And Arno Rauschenbeutel
abstract:
Author(s): Max Schemmer, Martin Cordier, Lucas Pache, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, and Arno Rauschenbeutel

We model and investigate the collective nonlinear optical response of an ensemble of two-level emitters that are weakly coupled to a waveguide featuring a single spatial mode. Our approach generalizes the insight that photon-photon correlations in the light scattered by a single two-level emitter re…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013711] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: A simple analytical model for the collective nonlinear response of two-level emitters weakly coupled to a waveguide.
motivation: To understand photon-photon correlations in waveguide QED with many emitters, which is relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.
method: Generalizes the single-emitter input-output formalism to an ensemble, deriving analytical expressions for second-order correlation functions.
result: The model captures collective effects such as superradiance and subradiance, and predicts non-classical photon statistics.
conclusion: The analytical model provides a useful tool for designing experiments with ensembles of emitters in waveguides.

title: Entanglement-entropy-based Scaling Relation In Qaoa Tensor Network Simulations For The Maxcut Problem
authors: Goro Miki And Yasuhiro Tokura
abstract:
Author(s): Goro Miki and Yasuhiro Tokura

With the rapid development of quantum computers in recent years, the importance of performance evaluation in quantum algorithms has been increasing. One method that has gained attention for performing this evaluation on classical computers is tensor networks. Tensor networks not only reduce the comp…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012610] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses tensor network simulations to study the entanglement entropy scaling in QAOA for MaxCut, proposing a scaling relation.
motivation: To evaluate quantum algorithms on classical computers efficiently using tensor networks and understand the role of entanglement in QAOA performance.
method: Tensor network simulations of QAOA for MaxCut on random graphs, analyzing entanglement entropy as a function of circuit depth and system size.
result: A scaling relation between entanglement entropy and QAOA depth is found, indicating limited entanglement growth.
conclusion: The scaling relation can help predict the classical simulability of QAOA and guide algorithm design.

title: Entanglement Dynamics In Minimal Kitaev Chains
authors: Vimalesh Kumar Vimal And Jorge Cayao
abstract:
Author(s): Vimalesh Kumar Vimal and Jorge Cayao

Minimal Kitaev chains host Majorana quasiparticles, which, although not topologically protected, exhibit spatial nonlocality and hence are expected to be useful for quantum information tasks. In this work, we consider two- and three-site Kitaev chains and investigate the dynamics of bipartite and mu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034308] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics in minimal Kitaev chains with two and three sites, focusing on Majorana quasiparticles.
motivation: Minimal Kitaev chains host Majorana quasiparticles with spatial nonlocality, which are expected to be useful for quantum information tasks.
method: The authors consider two- and three-site Kitaev chains and investigate the dynamics of bipartite and multipartite entanglement using appropriate measures.
result: The paper characterizes how entanglement evolves in these small systems, revealing features related to Majorana nonlocality.
conclusion: The work provides insights into entanglement properties of minimal Kitaev chains, but the systems are too small to have direct practical impact on quantum information processing.

title: Nonequilibrium Orders In Parametrically Driven Field Theories
authors: Carl Philipp Zelle, Romain Daviet, Andrew J. Millis, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Carl Philipp Zelle, Romain Daviet, Andrew J. Millis, and Sebastian Diehl

Driving quantum materials with coherent light has proven a powerful platform to realize a plethora of interesting phases and transitions, ranging from ferroelectricity to superconductivity and limit cycles in pumped magnonics. In this paper we develop the field theoretical framework to describe none…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024308] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Develops a field-theoretic framework for nonequilibrium orders in parametrically driven systems, focusing on limit cycles and phase transitions.
motivation: To understand and classify nonequilibrium phases induced by coherent driving in quantum materials, such as ferroelectricity and superconductivity.
method: Uses Keldysh field theory and renormalization group analysis to study driven-dissipative systems with parametric driving.
result: Identifies universal scaling behavior and phase diagrams for nonequilibrium orders, including limit cycles and time-crystalline phases.
conclusion: Provides a systematic framework for describing nonequilibrium phases in driven quantum materials, with implications for Floquet engineering and time crystals.

title: Access-limited Equilibration And Observable-dependent Relaxation In Lattice-gas Systems
authors: Marvin A. Albao
abstract:
Author(s): Marvin A. Albao

We investigate equilibration dynamics in a lattice-gas model with spatially restricted coupling to a particle reservoir. Using kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, we isolate the role of reservoir-access geometry by comparing spatially uniform exchange with exchange confined to a limited access region w…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014124] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies equilibration dynamics in a lattice-gas model with spatially restricted reservoir access using kinetic Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand how the geometry of reservoir coupling affects equilibration and relaxation in many-body systems.
method: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations comparing spatially uniform exchange with exchange confined to a limited access region.
result: The access-limited geometry leads to observable-dependent relaxation and non-exponential equilibration.
conclusion: Spatial restrictions on reservoir coupling can significantly alter equilibration dynamics, relevant for understanding non-equilibrium behavior in mesoscopic systems.

title: Control Protocols For Harmonically Confined Run-and-tumble Particles
authors: Marco Baldovin And Alessandro Manacorda
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Baldovin and Alessandro Manacorda

A run-and-tumble particle is placed in a harmonic confining potential, and an external agent can vary the tumbling rate and the strength of the trap over time. The objective is to find time-dependent control protocols steering the system between assigned end states, in a prescribed time interval. Under suitable assumptions, the authors find analytical solutions that are tested against simulations and provide insightful intuition.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014112] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives optimal control protocols for a run-and-tumble particle in a harmonic trap, minimizing work or maximizing efficiency.
motivation: Understanding how to control active particles is important for applications in microrobotics and biological systems, but the paper focuses on a specific model without clear connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analytically solve the optimal control problem for a run-and-tumble particle with time-dependent tumbling rate and trap stiffness, using a Fokker-Planck approach.
result: They find analytical protocols that steer the system between equilibrium states in finite time, and verify them with simulations.
conclusion: The work provides insight into control of active matter but does not address quantum effects or fundamental thermodynamic bounds on information processing.

title: Sequential Analysis In A Continuous Spin-noise Quantum Sensor
authors: E. Roda-Salichs, G. Gasbarri, A. Alou, M. Skotiniotis, A. Sierant, D. Méndez-Avalos, M. W. Mitchell, And J. Calsamiglia
abstract:
Author(s): E. Roda-Salichs, G. Gasbarri, A. Alou, M. Skotiniotis, A. Sierant, D. Méndez-Avalos, M. W. Mitchell, and J. Calsamiglia

Many control and detection applications require real-time analysis of signals from sensors, in order to quickly and accurately act upon events revealed by the sensors. Such signal analysis benefits from statistical models of signal and sensor behavior. This creates a need for data analysis methods t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033038] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a sequential analysis method for continuous spin-noise quantum sensors, enabling real-time detection of magnetic field changes.
motivation: Real-time analysis of sensor signals is needed for control and detection applications, but existing methods are not optimized for quantum sensors with continuous output.
method: The authors propose a sequential hypothesis testing framework that processes the continuous spin-noise signal to detect changes in the magnetic field, using a statistical model of the sensor's noise.
result: The method achieves faster detection times compared to fixed-sample-size approaches, with controlled error rates, demonstrated on a spin-noise sensor.
conclusion: Sequential analysis is effective for continuous quantum sensors, offering improved speed and accuracy for real-time monitoring tasks.

title: Learning Complexity Gradually In Quantum Machine Learning Models
authors: Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, And Carlos Bravo-Prieto
abstract:
Author(s): Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, and Carlos Bravo-Prieto

Quantum machine learning is an emergent field that continues to draw significant interest for its potential to offer improvements over classical algorithms in certain areas. However, training quantum models remains a challenging task, largely because of the difficulty in establishing an effective in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033006] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to gradually increase the expressivity of quantum machine learning models during training to improve optimization and generalization.
motivation: Training quantum machine learning models is challenging due to difficulties in establishing effective inductive biases and avoiding barren plateaus.
method: The authors introduce a training scheme that starts with a restricted model and progressively adds complexity, controlling the expressivity of the quantum circuit.
result: The gradual learning approach improves training convergence and generalization performance on benchmark tasks compared to standard training.
conclusion: Gradual complexity increase is a promising strategy for training quantum machine learning models, potentially mitigating issues like barren plateaus.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective explores how biomolecular condensation in living cells can process high-dimensional information through phase transitions.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, and biomolecular condensates may offer a powerful computational framework.
method: The authors propose that phase transitions in condensates enable high-dimensional sensing and classification, drawing analogies to physical computation.
result: They argue that condensates can implement computations like thresholding and classification, potentially more efficiently than molecular networks.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation is a promising paradigm for cellular information processing, warranting further theoretical and experimental study.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in quantum neural networks for continual learning, showing that quantum models maintain flexibility as parameters grow.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, while quantum neural networks may offer inherent advantages due to their parameter structure.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks theoretically and empirically, comparing plasticity retention with classical counterparts.
result: Quantum neural networks exhibit superior preservation of plasticity, enabling effective continual learning without explicit regularization.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks are promising for continual learning tasks due to their intrinsic plasticity, which could be leveraged for more adaptive AI systems.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but existing methods struggle with large multiqubit unitaries. The authors aim to extend the reach of stabilizer-based simulation by leveraging symmetries.
method: The authors develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for larger systems, combining group-theoretic methods with optimization.
result: They demonstrate that symmetry reductions enable classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits beyond previous limits, achieving significant speedups for certain structured unitaries.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for simulating near-Clifford circuits, though the approach is limited to circuits with sufficient symmetry and Clifford structure.

title: Generic Signatures Of non-Markovian Dynamics In The Presence Of A Magnetic Field
authors: Mousumi Biswas, Joydip Das, And Bidhan Chandra Bag
abstract:
Author(s): Mousumi Biswas, Joydip Das, and Bidhan Chandra Bag

In this paper, we have presented the three-dimensional dynamics in the velocity space of a Brownian particle coupled to a non-Markovian thermal bath in the presence of a magnetic field (MF), as well as external deterministic and stochastic force fields. The directions of the MF and the deterministic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014121] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-Markovian dynamics of a Brownian particle in a magnetic field, focusing on velocity-space signatures.
motivation: Understanding non-Markovian effects in the presence of a magnetic field is important for modeling realistic stochastic systems.
method: The authors derive a three-dimensional Langevin equation with memory kernel and solve it analytically for velocity correlation functions.
result: They find that the magnetic field induces oscillatory behavior in the velocity correlations, with non-Markovian effects leading to modified damping and frequency shifts.
conclusion: The work provides generic signatures of non-Markovian dynamics in magnetic fields, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Quantum-Error-Correction-Inspired Noise Mitigation For Wavelike Dark Matter Searches With Quantum Sensors
authors: Hajime Fukuda, Takeo Moroi, And Thanaporn Sichanugrist
abstract:
Author(s): Hajime Fukuda, Takeo Moroi, and Thanaporn Sichanugrist

We propose a quantum-error-correction-inspired noise mitigation protocol for enhancing the sensitivity of wavelike dark matter searches with quantum sensors. Our protocol uses multiple sensors to mitigate the noise affecting each sensor individually, allowing for the suppression of excitation noise …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021001] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum-error-correction-inspired noise mitigation protocol to improve sensitivity of wavelike dark matter searches using quantum sensors.
motivation: Wavelike dark matter searches with quantum sensors are limited by noise; existing noise mitigation techniques are insufficient.
method: Uses multiple quantum sensors and a protocol inspired by quantum error correction to suppress excitation noise affecting individual sensors.
result: The protocol enhances sensitivity for detecting wavelike dark matter signals beyond what is achievable with single sensors.
conclusion: Quantum error correction techniques can be adapted to improve quantum sensor performance in dark matter detection.

title: Quantum Stochastic Dynamics Of Nonlinear Driven Light Emission
authors: Philipp Stammer
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Stammer

This work extends quantum optical models of high harmonic generation towards open systems, by considering a quantum stochastic analysis of the field modes coupled to an environment. We study the open system dynamics by solving the quantum Langevin equation for a nonlinear driven cavity coupled to an…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013712] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: Extends quantum optical models of high harmonic generation to open systems using quantum stochastic dynamics and Langevin equations.
motivation: To understand the open system dynamics of nonlinear driven light emission, which is relevant for quantum optics and potentially quantum thermodynamics.
method: Solves the quantum Langevin equation for a nonlinear driven cavity coupled to an environment.
result: Provides a quantum stochastic analysis of the field modes, revealing the influence of the environment on the nonlinear emission.
conclusion: The work offers a framework for studying open quantum systems in nonlinear optics, but its direct connection to information thermodynamics is limited.

title: Limits Of Clifford Disentangling In Tensor Network States
authors: Sergi Masot-Llima, Piotr Sierant, Paolo Stornati, And Artur Garcia-Saez
abstract:
Author(s): Sergi Masot-Llima, Piotr Sierant, Paolo Stornati, and Artur Garcia-Saez

Tensor network methods leverage the limited entanglement of quantum states to efficiently simulate many-body systems. Alternatively, Clifford circuits provide a framework for handling highly entangled stabilizer states, which have low magic and are thus also classically tractable. Clifford tensor ne…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024311] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores the limits of using Clifford circuits to disentangle tensor network states, showing that Clifford disentangling is generally inefficient for generic quantum states.
motivation: Tensor network methods are limited by entanglement, while Clifford circuits can handle highly entangled stabilizer states with low magic. The authors aim to understand whether Clifford circuits can be used to disentangle tensor network states, potentially extending the reach of tensor network methods.
method: The authors analyze the structure of Clifford tensor networks and prove that the Clifford disentangling map is a tensor product of local Clifford unitaries, which cannot reduce entanglement beyond a certain point. They provide rigorous bounds on the entanglement entropy after Clifford disentangling.
result: They show that for generic quantum states, Clifford disentangling cannot reduce the entanglement entropy below a value that scales with the number of qubits, implying that Clifford circuits are not effective for disentangling arbitrary tensor network states.
conclusion: Clifford circuits are insufficient for disentangling generic tensor network states, limiting their use in improving tensor network simulations of many-body systems.

title: Majorana Zero Modes In Superconductor-magnet Heterostructures With $d$-wave Order
authors: Bastien Fajardo, T. Pereg-Barnea, Arun Paramekanti, And Kartiek Agarwal
abstract:
Author(s): Bastien Fajardo, T. Pereg-Barnea, Arun Paramekanti, and Kartiek Agarwal

Magnetic skyrmions in proximity to superconductors offer a route to engineering topological superconductivity due to the synthetic spin-orbit coupling engendered by the spin twist of the skyrmion texture. Previous theoretical works show that this leads to Majorana zero modes (MZMs) in skyrmion-vorte…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065117] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically predicts Majorana zero modes in skyrmion-superconductor heterostructures with d-wave order.
motivation: To engineer topological superconductivity and Majorana zero modes using magnetic skyrmions in proximity to d-wave superconductors.
method: The authors model a skyrmion texture coupled to a d-wave superconductor and solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations to find bound states.
result: They find that a skyrmion-vortex structure can host Majorana zero modes, with the d-wave order providing additional topological protection.
conclusion: Skyrmion-superconductor heterostructures are a promising platform for realizing Majorana zero modes, relevant for topological quantum computing.

title: Emergence Of Darcy's Law And Apparent Violation Of Onsager Symmetry In Multiphase Transport
authors: Omid Tavakkoli, Dick Bedeaux, Signe Kjelstrup, Steffen Berg, Marcel Moura, Ying Da Wang, Peyman Mostaghimi, And Ryan T. Armstrong
abstract:
Author(s): Omid Tavakkoli, Dick Bedeaux, Signe Kjelstrup, Steffen Berg, Marcel Moura, Ying Da Wang, Peyman Mostaghimi, and Ryan T. Armstrong

We introduce a nonequilibrium thermodynamic (NET) framework for immiscible two-phase flow in porous media, in which the total flux of both phases is driven by the gradient of an effective pressure. We show that the classical two-phase Darcy formulation emerges as a projected limit of the full linear…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015103] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a nonequilibrium thermodynamic framework for two-phase flow in porous media, showing that Darcy's law emerges from a linear force-flux relation and that Onsager symmetry appears violated due to coarse-graining.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic basis of multiphase transport in porous media and reconcile apparent violations of Onsager symmetry.
method: The authors apply nonequilibrium thermodynamics (NET) to immiscible two-phase flow, deriving flux equations from entropy production and projecting onto a reduced set of forces.
result: They demonstrate that the classical two-phase Darcy formulation is a projected limit of the full linear NET equations, and that the apparent violation of Onsager symmetry arises from the projection.
conclusion: The NET framework provides a consistent thermodynamic foundation for multiphase flow, explaining emergent behavior and symmetry violations.

title: Covariant Formulation Of The Berry Connection In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Ievgen I. Arkhipov
abstract:
Author(s): Ievgen I. Arkhipov

Non-Hermitian systems exhibit spectral and topological phenomena absent in Hermitian physics; however, their geometric characterization remains subtle due to the intrinsic ambiguity of biorthogonal eigenspaces. Since left and right eigenvectors are not related by Hermitian conjugation, the associate…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033037] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant formulation of the Berry connection for non-Hermitian systems, addressing the ambiguity in biorthogonal eigenspaces.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unique spectral and topological phenomena, but their geometric characterization is subtle due to the lack of Hermiticity. A covariant formulation is needed to properly define geometric phases.
method: The authors introduce a gauge-covariant Berry connection using a metric that accounts for the biorthogonality of left and right eigenvectors, and derive its transformation properties.
result: They obtain a well-defined geometric phase that is independent of the arbitrary scaling of eigenvectors, and demonstrate its application to a simple non-Hermitian model.
conclusion: The covariant formulation resolves the ambiguity in the Berry connection for non-Hermitian systems, providing a robust framework for studying topological effects in such systems.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in two dimensions is challenging because braiding of Abelian anyons is insufficient for universal gates; non-Abelian anyons offer a solution but are hard to realize.
method: The authors design a protocol that temporarily moves data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform complex logic gates, leveraging topological properties.
result: They demonstrate a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D without requiring complex braiding.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach to universal quantum computation in 2D, potentially simplifying hardware requirements.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires high overhead; the goal is to reduce both qubit and time overhead using advanced quantum error-correcting codes.
method: The authors employ parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques with good quantum LDPC codes to achieve efficient fault tolerance.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, significantly improving over conventional surface code approaches.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes enable more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation, bringing practical quantum computing closer.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is a key component for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing protocols have high overhead. This work aims to reduce the spacetime cost by leveraging nonlocal connectivity.
method: The authors propose a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states through transversal gates and lattice surgery techniques.
result: The protocol achieves significantly lower spacetime overhead compared to traditional magic state distillation methods, particularly in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a practical path toward low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for emerging quantum hardware with nonlocal interactions.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes achieves high accuracy and low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast enough for real-time operation, but existing decoders often trade off one for the other.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoder that explores a limited set of candidate error patterns, balancing search breadth and depth to achieve near-optimal decoding with low computational cost.
result: The decoder demonstrates high accuracy on quantum LDPC codes while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction, avoiding the need for massive classical resources.
conclusion: Beam search decoding is a practical solution for real-time quantum error correction, offering a favorable trade-off between accuracy and speed.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code using twisted color circuits and a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings requires efficient non-Clifford gate implementations.
method: Proposes twisted color circuits, a family of scalable circuits, and a just-in-time decoder to achieve fault tolerance.
result: Demonstrates a scalable approach for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code with planar geometry.
conclusion: The work advances fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar architectures, but is primarily a quantum error correction and fault tolerance contribution.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a need for clear criteria to assess the protection and feasibility of Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to define Majorana bound states in interacting systems and compute measures of robustness and locality.
result: They provide quantitative criteria to distinguish topologically protected Majorana states from trivial Andreev bound states in interacting settings.
conclusion: The work offers practical tools to evaluate Majorana-based qubit platforms, but the focus on topological qubit hardware is not a priority for the user's research interests.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, and Bao-Sen Shi

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian topological phenomena in a cold Rydberg gas platform.
motivation: Non-Hermitian topology is a new frontier in physics, and cold Rydberg gases offer a tunable dissipative many-body system to explore it.
method: The authors use a cold Rydberg gas as a dissipative platform and map out non-Hermitian spectral topology by measuring winding numbers and nonreciprocity.
result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity, confirming non-Hermitian topological behavior.
conclusion: Cold Rydberg gases are a viable platform for studying non-Hermitian topology, opening new avenues for topological physics in dissipative systems.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms, but the paper focuses on complexity classification rather than information-theoretic results.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using computational complexity theory, likely employing reductions and oracle separations.
result: They provide a complexity characterization that delineates when quantum computers can outperform classical ones for matrix function problems.
conclusion: The work offers insights into potential quantum advantage but is primarily a complexity-theoretic study, not directly advancing the researcher's core interests in quantum information theory.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a fault-tolerant quantum computing technique.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computation, so reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that exploits commuting structures in quantum circuits to reduce the number of T gates.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for T-count reduction, contributing to more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlation physics and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel metastable phases and functionalities.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory, time-resolved spectroscopy, and pump-probe techniques.
result: Key mechanisms for photodoping, thermalization, and emergence of metastable orders (superconducting, magnetic, etc.) are identified.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate correlated materials, but the field is still developing with many open questions.

title: Dynamics Of Squeezed Vacuum In Waveguide Arrays With Next-nearest-neighbor Coupling And Disorder
authors: Sunita Meena, Ankan Das Roy, Sugar Singh Meena, Amit Rai, And Gautam Vemuri
abstract:
Author(s): Sunita Meena, Ankan Das Roy, Sugar Singh Meena, Amit Rai, and Gautam Vemuri

We report the dynamics of a single-mode squeezed vacuum in evanescently coupled waveguide arrays incorporating next-nearest-neighbor coupling (NNNC) and disorder. Using an extended tight-binding framework, we show that NNNC reshapes the system's dispersion (phase), breaks spectral symmetry, and intr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013709] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of squeezed vacuum in waveguide arrays with next-nearest-neighbor coupling and disorder, focusing on dispersion and spectral properties.
motivation: Understanding how squeezed light propagates in disordered waveguide arrays with extended coupling is relevant for quantum optics and photonic quantum information processing.
method: The authors use an extended tight-binding model to analyze the effects of next-nearest-neighbor coupling and disorder on the dispersion relation and dynamics of squeezed vacuum.
result: Next-nearest-neighbor coupling reshapes the dispersion, breaks spectral symmetry, and introduces new features in the propagation dynamics.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into controlling quantum light propagation in engineered photonic structures, but the work is primarily a photonic platform study without direct information-theoretic results.

title: Physics-inspired Transformer Quantum States Via Latent Imaginary-time Evolution
authors: Kimihiro Yamazaki, Itsushi Sakata, Takuya Konishi, And Yoshinobu Kawahara
abstract:
Author(s): Kimihiro Yamazaki, Itsushi Sakata, Takuya Konishi, and Yoshinobu Kawahara

Neural quantum states (NQS) are powerful ansätze in the variational Monte Carlo framework, yet their architectures are often treated as black boxes. We propose a physically transparent framework in which NQS are treated as neural approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution. This viewpoint sugg…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033032] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a physically transparent framework for neural quantum states by interpreting them as approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution.
motivation: Neural quantum states are powerful but often treated as black boxes; the authors aim to provide a physically motivated architecture.
method: They introduce a framework where NQS are viewed as neural approximations to imaginary-time evolution, using a latent space and a variational Monte Carlo approach.
result: The framework yields competitive ground-state energies for spin models and offers interpretability through the latent dynamics.
conclusion: The approach bridges machine learning and quantum many-body physics, but the contribution is primarily computational and not directly advancing quantum information theory.

title: Toric Code Under Antiferromagnetic Isotropic Heisenberg Interactions
authors: Won Jang, Robert Peters, And Thore Posske
abstract:
Author(s): Won Jang, Robert Peters, and Thore Posske

We investigate the impact of an isotropic antiferromagnetic Heisenberg perturbation on the toric code, focusing on the resulting quantum phase transition and the nature of the phase that emerges beyond topological order. Using neural-network quantum states, we compute ground states over a wide range…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033008] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of an antiferromagnetic Heisenberg perturbation on the toric code, revealing a quantum phase transition from topological order to a trivial paramagnet.
motivation: Understanding the stability of topological order under perturbations is important for quantum error correction and condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use neural-network quantum states (NQS) to compute ground states of the perturbed toric code Hamiltonian for various perturbation strengths.
result: They find a first-order quantum phase transition at a critical perturbation strength, beyond which the system enters a trivial paramagnetic phase.
conclusion: The toric code's topological order is fragile against isotropic Heisenberg interactions, and the transition is first-order.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction with exponential convergence guarantees.
motivation: Belief propagation (BP) is a heuristic for tensor network contraction but lacks rigorous error bounds; the authors aim to provide systematic corrections to BP that yield polynomial-time algorithms with provable approximation guarantees.
method: The authors propose a cluster expansion approach that adds corrections to BP, leading to a family of algorithms with exponential convergence in the cluster size, and derive rigorous bounds on the approximation error.
result: The cluster-corrected BP algorithm achieves exponential convergence in the correction order, with polynomial computational cost, and outperforms standard BP on benchmark tensor networks.
conclusion: This work provides a theoretically grounded and practically efficient method for tensor network contraction, bridging the gap between heuristic BP and exact contraction methods.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis is proposed, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The paper presents a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and topological invariants to compute persistence diagrams more efficiently than classical methods.
result: The algorithm achieves a provable exponential speedup over the best known classical algorithms for certain instances of topological data analysis.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a potential quantum advantage in a practical application, though the practical relevance depends on the availability of fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant of knots with applications in quantum computing, but its approximation is classically hard, motivating the development of quantum algorithms.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm pipeline that includes state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They demonstrate the algorithm on small knots, showing that the quantum computation yields results consistent with theoretical predictions, and discuss resource requirements for scaling.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical benchmark for quantum computers and suggests potential quantum advantage for topological problems, but the contribution is primarily algorithmic and experimental rather than advancing quantum information theory.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and beyond.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm efficiently identifies hidden subgroups in Abelian groups from quantum states, with applications to learning stabilizer groups.
conclusion: This work provides a unified framework for symmetry learning in quantum information, but its focus is on quantum algorithms rather than the researcher's core interests in entanglement, thermodynamics, or quantum networks.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to model neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity to enable perception, thought, and action.
method: Uses maximum entropy models and renormalization group analysis on recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: Uncovers reproducible collective behaviors and demonstrates predictive power of statistical physics in neuroscience.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a quantitative framework for analyzing neural network data, bridging theory and experiment.

title: Truncated Photon
authors: Isak Cecil Onsager Rukan, Jan Gulla, And Johannes Skaar
abstract:
Author(s): Isak Cecil Onsager Rukan, Jan Gulla, and Johannes Skaar

Removing a mirror while a single photon is in the process of reflecting creates a quantum state of countless photons, theorists say.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033601] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of the quantum state created when a mirror is suddenly removed during photon reflection.
motivation: To understand the effect of a time-dependent boundary condition on a single photon, leading to multiphoton generation.
method: Analytical calculation of the quantum state after a sudden change in boundary conditions for a single-photon wavepacket.
result: The removal of the mirror transforms the single-photon state into a multi-photon state with a specific photon number distribution.
conclusion: The phenomenon illustrates fundamental aspects of quantum optics and boundary conditions, but has no direct application to the listed research directions.

title: Kondo Effect In Nonreciprocal Response
authors: Hajime Murata And Hiroaki Ishizuka
abstract:
Author(s): Hajime Murata and Hiroaki Ishizuka

Chiral magnetic states give rise to rich phenomena, from the anomalous Hall effect and the nonlinear electrical current to multiferroics and magnetochiral dichroism. Most of the studies on electrical transport so far have focused on the cases where the magnetic moments are well approximated by class…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036301] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Kondo effect in nonreciprocal transport in chiral magnets, focusing on electrical transport phenomena.
motivation: Chiral magnetic states exhibit rich transport phenomena, but the role of the Kondo effect in nonreciprocal response has not been explored.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the Kondo effect in a chiral magnet using a microscopic model and calculate the nonreciprocal conductivity.
result: They find that the Kondo effect can significantly enhance nonreciprocal response, leading to a characteristic temperature dependence.
conclusion: The Kondo effect is an important mechanism for nonreciprocal transport in chiral magnets, offering new insights into magnetochiral phenomena.

title: Nonlinear Odd Viscoelastic Effect
authors: Ashwat Jain, Wojciech J. Jankowski, M. Mehraeen, And Robert-Jan Slager
abstract:
Author(s): Ashwat Jain, Wojciech J. Jankowski, M. Mehraeen, and Robert-Jan Slager

Nonlinear odd viscoelastic effects arise from higher-order quantum geometric tensors in magnetic three-dimensional topological phases in response to distortion fields.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036302] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonlinear odd viscoelastic effects arising from higher-order quantum geometric tensors in magnetic topological phases.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum geometry and viscoelastic response in topological materials.
method: Theoretical analysis using higher-order quantum geometric tensors and response theory for distortion fields.
result: Prediction of nonlinear odd viscoelastic effects in magnetic three-dimensional topological phases.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of viscoelasticity in quantum materials, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Demonstration Of Deuterium’s Enhanced Sensitivity To Symmetry Violations Governed By The Standard-Model Extension
authors: A. Nanda, D. Comparat, O. Dulieu, S. Lahs, C. Malbrunot, L. Nowak, M. C. Simon, And E. Widmann
abstract:
Author(s): A. Nanda, D. Comparat, O. Dulieu, S. Lahs, C. Malbrunot, L. Nowak, M. C. Simon, and E. Widmann

We have performed hyperfine spectroscopy of two transitions in ground-state deuterium and searched for violations of [MATH] and Lorentz symmetry that would manifest as sidereal variations of the observed transition frequencies. Several nonrelativistic proton coefficients of the Standard-Model extensi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 031802] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper tests Lorentz and CPT symmetry violations in deuterium using hyperfine spectroscopy, but does not align with the specified research directions.
motivation: To search for violations of Lorentz and CPT symmetry in deuterium, which could indicate physics beyond the Standard Model.
method: Hyperfine spectroscopy of two transitions in ground-state deuterium, searching for sidereal variations in transition frequencies.
result: Constraints on nonrelativistic proton coefficients of the Standard-Model Extension were obtained.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates enhanced sensitivity to symmetry violations in deuterium, but no violations were observed.

title: Atomic Clock Frequency Ratios With Fractional Uncertainty $≤3.2×{10}^{−18}$
authors: Alexander Aeppli et Al.
