title: Holographic Aspects Of Dynamical Mean-field Theory
authors: Kouichi Okunishi And Akihisa Koga
abstract:
Author(s): Kouichi Okunishi and Akihisa Koga

Dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) is one of the most standard theoretical frameworks for addressing strongly correlated electron systems. In this study, we explore a holographic renormalization-group (RG)-like structure inherent in DMFT, which we refer to as “AdS/DMFT,” by focusing on the backgroun…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065114] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores a holographic renormalization-group-like structure in dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for strongly correlated electron systems.
motivation: To understand the connection between DMFT and holographic duality (AdS/CFT) and to develop a new perspective on strongly correlated systems.
method: The authors analyze the background structure of DMFT and draw analogies with the holographic renormalization group, proposing an 'AdS/DMFT' correspondence.
result: They identify a holographic RG-like structure inherent in DMFT, suggesting a duality between DMFT and a gravitational theory in one higher dimension.
conclusion: The work provides a conceptual bridge between condensed matter theory and holography, but does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fragility Of Local Moments Against Hybridization With Flat Bands
authors: Max Fischer, Arianna Poli, Lorenzo Crippa, Dumitru Călugăru, Sergio Ciuchi, Matthias Vojta, Alessandro Toschi, And Giorgio Sangiovanni
abstract:
Author(s): Max Fischer, Arianna Poli, Lorenzo Crippa, Dumitru Călugăru, Sergio Ciuchi, Matthias Vojta, Alessandro Toschi, and Giorgio Sangiovanni

The Kondo screening of a localized magnetic moment crucially depends on the spectral properties of the electronic bath to which it is coupled. Unlike textbook examples, realistic systems as well as dynamical mean-field theory of correlated lattice models force us to consider sharp features in the hy…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065115] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Kondo screening of local magnetic moments coupled to flat-band electronic baths, focusing on the fragility of local moments due to hybridization with flat bands.
motivation: Understanding how sharp features in the electronic density of states, such as flat bands, affect Kondo screening is important for correlated lattice models and realistic materials.
method: The authors use analytical and numerical methods, likely including dynamical mean-field theory or impurity solvers, to analyze the Kondo model with a flat-band bath.
result: They find that local moments are fragile against hybridization with flat bands, leading to suppressed Kondo screening or altered screening behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between flat bands and Kondo physics, relevant for strongly correlated electron systems.

title: Spin-valley Matching Mechanisms In High-performance Multiferroic Tunnel Junctions
authors: Zhi Yang, Bao-Fu Ruan, Min Li, Bing-Xin Liu, Chuan-Kui Wang, Zong-Liang Li, And Shuai Qiu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi Yang, Bao-Fu Ruan, Min Li, Bing-Xin Liu, Chuan-Kui Wang, Zong-Liang Li, and Shuai Qiu

Multiferroic tunnel junctions (MFTJs) with tunneling electroresistance (TER) and tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) effects have emerged as promising candidates for low-power and high-density information technology. However, simultaneously achieving giant TER and TMR ratios still faces significant hu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065303] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-valley matching mechanisms in multiferroic tunnel junctions to achieve giant tunneling electroresistance and magnetoresistance.
motivation: Multiferroic tunnel junctions are promising for low-power, high-density information technology, but simultaneously achieving giant TER and TMR ratios remains challenging.
method: The authors investigate spin-valley matching mechanisms using first-principles calculations or device modeling (details not fully provided in abstract).
result: They identify mechanisms that enable high TER and TMR ratios simultaneously.
conclusion: The work provides insights for designing high-performance multiferroic tunnel junctions for information storage.

title: Unconventional Spin Valve Based On Normal Metal/chiral Molecule/altermagnet Junctions
authors: Tian-Yi Zhang, Peng-Yi Liu, Yu-Fei Sun, Ai-Min Guo, And Qing-Feng Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Tian-Yi Zhang, Peng-Yi Liu, Yu-Fei Sun, Ai-Min Guo, and Qing-Feng Sun

Chiral molecules have attracted broad interdisciplinary interest for their ability to produce highly spin-polarized current. This phenomenon, known as the chiral-induced spin-selectivity effect, holds great potential in the field of spintronics. Here, we propose combining chiral molecules with alter…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065412] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a spin valve combining chiral molecules with altermagnets, focusing on spintronic device physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Chiral molecules exhibit spin-selective transport, and altermagnets offer unique spin properties; combining them could enable novel spintronic devices.
method: The authors theoretically model a normal metal/chiral molecule/altermagnet junction and calculate spin transport properties using scattering theory.
result: They predict a large spin valve effect with high magnetoresistance ratio due to the interplay of chiral-induced spin selectivity and altermagnet band structure.
conclusion: The proposed device may be useful for spintronic applications, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Weak Localization And Antilocalization Corrections To Nonlinear Transport: A Semiclassical Boltzmann Treatment
authors: Dmitry V. Chichinadze
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitry V. Chichinadze

The nonlinear transport regime is manifested in the nonlinear current-voltage characteristic of the system. An example of such a nonlinear regime is a setup in which current is injected into the sample and the measured voltage drop is quadratic in the injected current. Such a quadratic nonlinear reg…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065413] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies weak localization and antilocalization corrections to nonlinear transport in disordered systems using a semiclassical Boltzmann approach.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear transport regimes is important for characterizing electronic properties of materials, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a semiclassical Boltzmann treatment to compute weak localization and antilocalization corrections to the nonlinear current-voltage characteristic.
result: They derive analytical expressions for the nonlinear conductivity corrections due to quantum interference effects.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for nonlinear transport in disordered systems, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nanobubble Superstructure: A Tuneable Grid Of Molecule Clusters In Twisted Bilayer Graphene
authors: Liye Fu, Yuerui Lu, And Juan F. Torres
abstract:
Author(s): Liye Fu, Yuerui Lu, and Juan F. Torres

Highly dense and ordered nanobubble arrays in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures are crucial for strain engineering electronic devices, fabricating high-capacity energy storage systems, and creating quantum emitters. However, neighboring nanobubbles have been found to spontaneously coalesce becaus…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065414] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the formation of a tunable nanobubble superstructure in twisted bilayer graphene, enabling ordered molecule clusters.
motivation: Nanobubble arrays in van der Waals heterostructures are important for strain engineering, energy storage, and quantum emitters, but coalescence limits their density and order.
method: The authors use twisted bilayer graphene to create a moiré pattern that templates the formation of highly dense and ordered nanobubble arrays, characterized by atomic force microscopy and theoretical modeling.
result: They demonstrate a tunable grid of molecule clusters with controlled size and spacing, overcoming the coalescence problem.
conclusion: This nanobubble superstructure provides a platform for strain engineering and quantum emitter applications.

title: Quantum Disorder Engineering In Superconducting Ti(O,N) Thin Films
authors: Fengmiao Li, Solveig Aamlid, Oliver A. Dicks, Myung-Geun Han, Giorgio Levy, Ronny Sutarto, Zhihao Chen, Chong Liu, Hsiang-Hsi Kung, Simon Godin, Bruce A. Davidson, Zhi Gang Cheng, Andrea Damascelli, Yimei Zhu, Christoph Heil, Ilya Elfimov, George A. Sawatzky, And Ke Zou
abstract:
Author(s): Fengmiao Li, Solveig Aamlid, Oliver A. Dicks, Myung-Geun Han, Giorgio Levy, Ronny Sutarto, Zhihao Chen, Chong Liu, Hsiang-Hsi Kung, Simon Godin, Bruce A. Davidson, Zhi Gang Cheng, Andrea Damascelli, Yimei Zhu, Christoph Heil, Ilya Elfimov, George A. Sawatzky, and Ke Zou

Nitrogen substitution for oxygen is an anion-engineering strategy for tailoring the rich physical properties of oxides. In this work, we investigate the effect of nitrogen doping in titanium monoxide (TiO) and the underlying mechanism, utilizing epitaxial titanium oxynitride Ti(O,N) films grown usin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065415] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nitrogen doping in titanium monoxide thin films to engineer disorder and tune superconducting properties.
motivation: To understand how anion substitution (nitrogen for oxygen) affects the physical properties of oxides, specifically superconductivity in titanium oxynitride films.
method: Epitaxial Ti(O,N) thin films were grown and characterized using various experimental techniques to probe structural and electronic changes.
result: Nitrogen doping introduces disorder and modifies the superconducting transition temperature and other properties.
conclusion: Anion engineering via nitrogen substitution is a viable strategy to tailor superconductivity in oxide films.

title: Distance Function For Stochastic Matrices
authors: Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, And Iain B. Styles
abstract:
Author(s): Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, and Iain B. Styles

The ability to quantify the similarity of stochastic processes is important in a wide range of areas including communications, simulation, and operational research. Such processes are commonly modeled as Markov Chains and so a natural way to compare their similarity is to compute distances between p…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014125] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a distance function for stochastic matrices based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate for Markov chains.
motivation: Quantifying similarity between stochastic processes is important in communications, simulation, and operational research, but existing distance measures for Markov chains have limitations.
method: The authors define a distance function using the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate between Markov chains and prove it satisfies metric properties.
result: The proposed distance function is a valid metric and can be computed efficiently for ergodic Markov chains.
conclusion: The distance function provides a principled way to compare stochastic processes modeled as Markov chains, with potential applications in clustering and classification.

title: Intermediate Scattering Function Of Brownian Particles In A Tilted Cosine Potential
authors: Regina Rusch And Thomas Franosch
abstract:
Author(s): Regina Rusch and Thomas Franosch

We solve the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derive the intermediate scattering function (ISF), which captures the full spatiotemporal dynamics of the system. The model consists of a single overdamped Brownian particle in one dimension. We derive a gen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014127] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derives the intermediate scattering function.
motivation: Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of Brownian particles in periodic potentials is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation analytically and numerically to obtain the intermediate scattering function for an overdamped Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential.
result: They derive a general expression for the ISF and analyze its dependence on tilt and potential strength.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed classical statistical mechanics result with no quantum or information-theoretic implications.

title: Floquet Resonances In The Double Kicked Top
authors: Avadhut V. Purohit And Udaysinh T. Bhosale
abstract:
Author(s): Avadhut V. Purohit and Udaysinh T. Bhosale

We study exact quantum resonances in the double kicked top (DKT), a driven spin model that extends the quantum kicked top (QKT) by introducing an additional time-reversal symmetry-breaking kick. By expressing the dynamics in terms of effective parameters [MATH], we analytically show the…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014214] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exact quantum resonances in a driven spin model called the double kicked top.
motivation: To understand quantum resonance phenomena in a periodically driven system with broken time-reversal symmetry.
method: Analytical derivation of effective parameters and analysis of the Floquet operator.
result: Exact conditions for quantum resonances are derived and characterized.
conclusion: The double kicked top exhibits rich resonance behavior that can be analytically understood.

title: Emergence Of Higher-order Interactions In Systems Of Coupled Kuramoto Oscillators With Time Delay
authors: Narumi Fujii, Keisuke Taga, Riccardo Muolo, Bob Rink, And Hiroya Nakao
abstract:
Author(s): Narumi Fujii, Keisuke Taga, Riccardo Muolo, Bob Rink, and Hiroya Nakao

We show that higher-order interactions naturally emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling in Kuramoto oscillators. By expanding the delayed pairwise coupling to the second order, we derive a delay-free Kuramoto model possessing both pairwise and three-body interactions. Numerical simulations and s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014215] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that higher-order interactions emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling in Kuramoto oscillators.
motivation: To understand how higher-order interactions can arise from simple pairwise couplings with time delay in oscillator networks.
method: Expands the delayed pairwise coupling to second order to derive a delay-free Kuramoto model with pairwise and three-body interactions, then performs numerical simulations and stability analysis.
result: The derived model exhibits novel collective dynamics, including multistability and chimera states, that are absent in the standard Kuramoto model.
conclusion: Time-delayed coupling can effectively generate higher-order interactions, providing a mechanism for complex dynamics in oscillator networks.

title: Dynamical Origin Of Extreme Events In Mutually Coupled And Networked Brusselator
authors: S. V. Manivelan, S. Sabarathinam, K. Thamilmaran, And I. Manimehan
abstract:
Author(s): S. V. Manivelan, S. Sabarathinam, K. Thamilmaran, and I. Manimehan

This study investigates the dynamical origins and statistical properties of extreme events (EEs) in a diffusively coupled theoretical Brusselator system, extending from pairwise interactions to globally coupled networks. Statistically, the emergence of EEs is characterized by heavy-tailed probabilit…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014217] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies extreme events in coupled Brusselator systems, a topic in nonlinear dynamics and complex systems.
motivation: Understanding the dynamical origin of extreme events in coupled chemical oscillators is important for predicting rare but impactful events.
method: The authors analyze a diffusively coupled Brusselator model, from pairwise to globally coupled networks, using statistical and dynamical systems tools.
result: They characterize extreme events by heavy-tailed probability distributions and identify dynamical mechanisms leading to their emergence.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the generation of extreme events in coupled nonlinear systems, with potential applications in various fields.

title: Different Phases And Phase Transition Points In Hidden Markov Models
authors: Ruben Poghosyan, Vardan Bardakhchyan, And David B. Saakian
abstract:
Author(s): Ruben Poghosyan, Vardan Bardakhchyan, and David B. Saakian

We are looking for different phases in hidden Markov models (HMMs). By analyzing the stationary solution of the master equation, we discover different situations with localized or delocalized distributions for the stationary distributions of the master equation. We hypothesize that these phases are …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014123] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phases and phase transitions in hidden Markov models using master equation analysis.
motivation: To identify different phases (localized vs delocalized) in hidden Markov models and understand their stationary distributions.
method: Analyzes the stationary solution of the master equation for hidden Markov models.
result: Discovers different phases with localized or delocalized stationary distributions and hypothesizes phase transition points.
conclusion: The work provides a classification of phases in HMMs but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Statistical Mechanics Of Indistinguishable Energy States And The Glass Transition
authors: Shimul Akhanjee
abstract:
Author(s): Shimul Akhanjee

The statistical mechanics of particles that populate indistinguishable energy substates is explored. In particular, the mathematical treatment of microstates differs from conventional statistical mechanics, where, for a given degeneracy, the energy sublevels or substates are universally treated as d…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014119] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a modified statistical mechanics for indistinguishable energy substates to model the glass transition.
motivation: Standard statistical mechanics treats degenerate energy levels as distinguishable, which may not capture the physics of glassy systems where substates are indistinguishable.
method: The author develops a mathematical framework where microstates are counted differently for indistinguishable energy substates, altering the partition function and thermodynamic quantities.
result: The new formalism predicts a thermodynamic singularity associated with the glass transition, offering a potential explanation for the observed behavior.
conclusion: The approach provides a novel statistical mechanical basis for understanding glass transitions, though it remains theoretical and requires experimental validation.

title: Twisted State Stability Under Local Order Parameter Adaptation
authors: Xueqin Wang, Hong He, Wende Tang, Yiju Peng, And Ya Jia
abstract:
Author(s): Xueqin Wang, Hong He, Wende Tang, Yiju Peng, and Ya Jia

Twisted states commonly arise in nonlocally coupled ring networks. We study the stability of twisted states in networks with higher-order interactions under the adaptive mechanism based on the local order parameter. The adaptive feedback dynamically regulates the coupling strength and thus reshapes …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014209] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of twisted states in nonlocally coupled ring networks with higher-order interactions and adaptive coupling based on local order parameters.
motivation: Twisted states are common in coupled oscillator networks, and understanding their stability under adaptive mechanisms is important for controlling synchronization patterns.
method: The authors analyze a ring network of phase oscillators with higher-order (simplicial) interactions and introduce an adaptive feedback that adjusts coupling strengths based on the local order parameter. They perform linear stability analysis and numerical simulations.
result: They derive stability conditions for twisted states and show that the adaptive mechanism can stabilize or destabilize certain twisted states depending on parameters.
conclusion: The adaptive coupling based on local order parameter provides a way to control the stability of twisted states in networks with higher-order interactions.

title: Energy-dynamics Interplay In Temporal Networks Triggers Explosive Synchronization
authors: Romuald Mbonwouo, Steve J. Kongni, Sishu Shankar Muni, Carmel T. Lambu, Venceslas Nguefoue, Patrick Louodop, And Thierry Njougouo
abstract:
Author(s): Romuald Mbonwouo, Steve J. Kongni, Sishu Shankar Muni, Carmel T. Lambu, Venceslas Nguefoue, Patrick Louodop, and Thierry Njougouo

Synchronization in networks of coupled oscillators is a fundamental problem in the study of collective behavior. In this paper we investigate the synchronization transition in networks of coupled dynamical systems from an energetic perspective. Interactions between systems/oscillators are assumed to…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014210] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies explosive synchronization in temporal networks from an energetic perspective, focusing on coupled oscillators.
motivation: Understanding synchronization transitions in networks is fundamental to collective behavior, and an energetic approach may reveal new mechanisms.
method: The authors model interactions between oscillators with energy dynamics and analyze synchronization transitions in temporal networks.
result: They find that the interplay between energy and network dynamics triggers explosive synchronization.
conclusion: The energetic perspective provides insights into synchronization phenomena in complex networks.

title: Quantum Nanorotator In The Hypomagnetic Field: Implications For Magnetobiology
authors: V. N. Binhi
abstract:
Author(s): V. N. Binhi

A mechanism for the biological effects of the hypomagnetic field is proposed, based on the rotational motion of a molecule as a whole within a cavity in an enzyme. It has been shown previously that a molecular rotator about 1 nm in size can have a decoherence time of up to tens of milliseconds. On s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014406] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum nanorotator mechanism for biological effects of hypomagnetic fields.
motivation: To explain how weak magnetic fields can affect biological systems, which is not well understood.
method: Models a molecule rotating within an enzyme cavity as a quantum rotator, analyzing decoherence and dynamics.
result: Shows that such a rotator can have long decoherence times and may be sensitive to hypomagnetic fields.
conclusion: The quantum nanorotator could be a plausible mechanism for magnetobiology, but the work is speculative and not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Polarization Conversion In Time-modulated Magnetized Plasmas: Faraday Configuration
authors: Hossein Mehrpour Bernety, Dikshitulu K. Kalluri, And Mark A. Cappelli
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Mehrpour Bernety, Dikshitulu K. Kalluri, and Mark A. Cappelli

In this paper, we address the problem of wave propagation within an unbounded time-modulated magnetized plasma in a Faraday configuration. We present an analysis formulated by coupling Maxwell's equations with the hydrodynamic evolution equation for the plasma current density, and casting the result…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015210] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave propagation in time-modulated magnetized plasmas, focusing on polarization conversion in the Faraday configuration.
motivation: Understanding wave propagation in time-varying plasmas is important for applications in plasma-based devices and communications.
method: The authors couple Maxwell's equations with the hydrodynamic plasma current density equation and solve for wave behavior under time modulation.
result: They analyze polarization conversion effects due to time modulation of the plasma parameters.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insights into wave-plasma interactions but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Autoparametric Excitation Of An Elastic Chain In A Periodic Potential
authors: Johann Maddi, Christophe Coste, And Michel Saint Jean
abstract:
Author(s): Johann Maddi, Christophe Coste, and Michel Saint Jean

We describe the motions of an elastic chain submitted to an external periodic potential, without dissipation. Initially, the energy is injected in a single eigenmode of the chain. We show that this eigenmode acts as a parametric forcing of the other modes, and since there is no external energy sourc…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015504] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the autoparametric excitation of an elastic chain in a periodic potential without dissipation, focusing on energy transfer between eigenmodes.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear dynamics and energy redistribution in elastic systems under periodic potentials.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of an elastic chain model where energy is initially injected into a single eigenmode, leading to parametric forcing of other modes.
result: The injected eigenmode acts as a parametric pump, transferring energy to other modes, and the system exhibits complex nonlinear behavior.
conclusion: The study reveals mechanisms of energy transfer in elastic chains, relevant to mechanical systems but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Structure And Memory Control Self-diffusion In Active Matter
authors: Akinlade Akintunde And Stewart A. Mallory
abstract:
Author(s): Akinlade Akintunde and Stewart A. Mallory

Despite extensive progress in characterizing the emergent behavior of active matter, the microscopic origins of self-diffusion in interacting active systems remain poorly understood. Here, we develop a framework that quantitatively links self-diffusion to collisional forces and their temporal correl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014115] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a framework linking self-diffusion to collisional forces in active matter, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding microscopic origins of self-diffusion in interacting active systems is poorly understood.
method: A theoretical framework that quantitatively links self-diffusion to collisional forces and their temporal correlations.
result: The framework provides a quantitative link between structure, memory, and self-diffusion in active matter.
conclusion: The study advances understanding of active matter but is outside the specified research interests.

title: Information Temperature And Macroscopic Descriptors Of Additive $N\text{th}$-order Markov Chains
authors: O. V. Usatenko, G. M. Pritula, And S. S. Melnyk
abstract:
Author(s): O. V. Usatenko, G. M. Pritula, and S. S. Melnyk

Large-scale language models (LLMs) operate in extremely high-dimensional state spaces, where both token embeddings and their hidden representations create complex dependences that are not easily reduced to classical Markov structures. In this paper we explore a theoretically solvable approximation o…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014116] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a solvable Markov chain model to approximate the high-dimensional state spaces of large language models, defining an information temperature and macroscopic descriptors.
motivation: Large language models operate in extremely high-dimensional spaces with complex dependencies that are not easily reduced to classical Markov structures, motivating a simplified theoretical model.
method: The authors propose an additive Nth-order Markov chain as a tractable approximation and define an information temperature based on the entropy of the chain.
result: They derive macroscopic descriptors such as information temperature and correlation functions for the model, providing analytical insights into the statistical properties.
conclusion: The model offers a theoretical framework for understanding some aspects of LLM behavior, but its applicability to real LLMs is limited due to the simplifying assumptions.

title: Topological Transitions In Swarmalators Systems
authors: Patrick Louodop, Michael N. Jipdi, Gael R. Simo, Steve J. Kongni, Carmel Lambu, Thierry Njougouo, Pablo D. Mininni, Kevin O'keeffe, And Hilda A. Cerdeira
abstract:
Author(s): Patrick Louodop, Michael N. Jipdi, Gael R. Simo, Steve J. Kongni, Carmel Lambu, Thierry Njougouo, Pablo D. Mininni, Kevin O'Keeffe, and Hilda A. Cerdeira

After its development, the swarmalators model attracted a great deal of attention since it was found to be very suitable to reproduce several behaviors in collective dynamics. However, few works explain the transitions that are observed while varying system parameters. In this letter, we demonstrate…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012201] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological transitions in swarmalator systems, which are models of collective dynamics combining synchronization and swarming.
motivation: Understanding the transitions observed in swarmalator systems as parameters vary is important for explaining emergent behaviors in collective dynamics.
method: The authors analyze a swarmalator model and demonstrate topological transitions through numerical simulations and theoretical analysis.
result: They identify and characterize topological transitions that occur as system parameters are varied.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the phase transitions of swarmalator systems, contributing to the understanding of collective behavior.

title: Percolation And Criticality Of Systems With Competing Interactions On Bethe Lattices: Limitations And Potential Strengths Of Cluster Schemes
authors: Greivin Alfaro Miranda, Mingyuan Zheng, Patrick Charbonneau, Antonio Coniglio, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, And Marco Tarzia
abstract:
Author(s): Greivin Alfaro Miranda, Mingyuan Zheng, Patrick Charbonneau, Antonio Coniglio, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, and Marco Tarzia

Cluster-based algorithms have led to remarkably efficient Monte Carlo sampling schemes that reduce critical slowing down. The authors demonstrate that seeking such cluster schemes for frustrated systems is futile, but they leave open the possibility that alternate approaches could be devised.

#TechnicalAdvancement #ClearMotivation


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014114] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies percolation and criticality in systems with competing interactions on Bethe lattices, focusing on the limitations of cluster Monte Carlo algorithms for frustrated systems.
motivation: Cluster algorithms reduce critical slowing down in Monte Carlo simulations, but their effectiveness for frustrated systems is unclear. The authors aim to determine whether such schemes can be devised for systems with competing interactions.
method: The authors analyze cluster-based Monte Carlo algorithms on Bethe lattices with competing interactions, examining the percolation and critical behavior to assess the feasibility of cluster schemes.
result: They demonstrate that seeking cluster schemes for frustrated systems is futile, but leave open the possibility that alternate approaches could be devised.
conclusion: Cluster algorithms are not effective for frustrated systems on Bethe lattices, but alternative methods may still be possible.

title: Stability Of Delay-coupled Reaction-diffusion Systems With Turing Or Wave Instability
authors: Keiji Konishi, Koki Yoshida, Yoshiki Sugitani, And Naoyuki Hara
abstract:
Author(s): Keiji Konishi, Koki Yoshida, Yoshiki Sugitani, and Naoyuki Hara

A quenching phenomenon that emerges in coupled oscillators, namely, amplitude death (AD), has been widely accepted. The present paper analytically deals with AD in two identical reaction-diffusion systems with periodic boundary or zero-flux boundary conditions that are coupled by a diffusive connect…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014207] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies amplitude death in delay-coupled reaction-diffusion systems with Turing or wave instability.
motivation: Understanding amplitude death in coupled oscillators is important for controlling oscillations in biological and chemical systems.
method: The authors analytically investigate two identical reaction-diffusion systems with diffusive coupling under periodic or zero-flux boundary conditions.
result: They derive conditions for amplitude death and analyze the effects of delay and coupling strength.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insights into stabilization of reaction-diffusion systems via coupling and delay.

title: Riding The Wave: Polymers In Time-dependent Nonequilibrium Baths
authors: Bhavesh Valecha, Jens-Uwe Sommer, And Abhinav Sharma
abstract:
Author(s): Bhavesh Valecha, Jens-Uwe Sommer, and Abhinav Sharma

Directed transport is a characteristic feature of numerous biological systems in response to signals such as nutrient and chemical gradients. These signals often depend on time owing to the high complexity of interactions in these systems. In this study, we focus on the steady-state behavior of poly…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015408] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies directed transport of polymers in time-dependent nonequilibrium baths, focusing on steady-state behavior.
motivation: Biological systems often exhibit directed transport in response to time-dependent signals, but the behavior of polymers in such baths is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze the steady-state behavior of polymers in time-dependent nonequilibrium baths using theoretical modeling.
result: The study reveals how polymers achieve directed transport in response to time-dependent signals.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into polymer dynamics in complex biological environments.

title: From Active To Odd To Smart Matter
authors: Olivier Dauchot
abstract:
Author(s): Olivier Dauchot

Active matter taught us that microscopic energy injection can lead to macroscopic dynamical order. Odd elasticity revealed that active solids can turn deformation into work. The next question is sharper: can matter learn what it is good for?


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 011001] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses the evolution of active matter research towards 'smart matter' that can learn and adapt, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The author aims to outline a future direction for active matter where materials can learn and perform useful functions, moving beyond current understanding of active and odd elastic matter.
method: The paper is a perspective or commentary, likely reviewing concepts from active matter and odd elasticity and proposing a new research agenda for smart matter.
result: No specific technical results are presented; the paper is forward-looking and conceptual.
conclusion: The next frontier in active matter is to create materials that can learn and adapt, integrating information processing with mechanical properties.

title: Interaction Of Solitons With Saturable Gain
authors: Akhilesh K. S. And Omri Gat
abstract:
Author(s): Akhilesh K. S. and Omri Gat

We study the tail-overlap interaction of a well-separated pair of dissipative solitons in systems with slow saturable gain. Gain saturation introduces nonlocal terms in the soliton field equation that depend on the total energy and therefore invalidate the standard methods used to study overlap inte…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014205] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interaction of dissipative solitons in systems with slow saturable gain, focusing on tail-overlap effects.
motivation: Understanding soliton interactions is important for applications in nonlinear optics and laser systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating nonlocal terms due to gain saturation and analyze the interaction dynamics.
result: They find that gain saturation introduces nonlocal effects that modify the standard soliton interaction picture.
conclusion: The work contributes to nonlinear wave theory but has no relevance to the specified research interests.

title: Eigenvector Localization And Universal Regime Transitions In Multiplex Networks: A Perturbative Approach
authors: Joan Hernàndez Tey And Emanuele Cozzo
abstract:
Author(s): Joan Hernàndez Tey and Emanuele Cozzo

We study the transition between layer-localized and delocalized regimes in a general contact-based contagion model on multiplex networks. Using the inverse participation ratio, we characterize how activity shifts from being confined to a single layer to spreading across the entire system. Through a …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014307] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies eigenvector localization and regime transitions in multiplex networks using a perturbative approach, applied to contagion models.
motivation: To understand how activity spreads across layers in multiplex networks and characterize the transition between localized and delocalized regimes.
method: Uses the inverse participation ratio and perturbative analysis to study eigenvector localization in multiplex networks.
result: Identifies universal regime transitions between layer-localized and delocalized phases in contact-based contagion models.
conclusion: The perturbative approach effectively captures the localization-delocalization transition, with implications for network dynamics.

title: Shell Formation And Two-dimensional Nanofriction In Three-dimensional Ion Coulomb Crystals
authors: L. A. Rüffert And T. E. Mehlstäubler
abstract:
Author(s): L. A. Rüffert and T. E. Mehlstäubler

Self-organized three-dimensional (3D) ion Coulomb crystals in linear Paul traps naturally form concentric shells that provide a curved, atomically resolved interface for studying two-dimensional (2D) nanofriction. Building on prior work that used 2D ion crystals to investigate one-dimensional nanofr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033044] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shell formation and nanofriction in 3D ion Coulomb crystals, which is a topic in classical or mesoscopic physics with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding nanofriction at curved interfaces using self-organized ion crystals.
method: Experimental and theoretical study of 3D ion Coulomb crystals in a linear Paul trap, observing shell structures and measuring friction.
result: Observation of concentric shells and characterization of two-dimensional nanofriction.
conclusion: Ion Coulomb crystals provide a platform for studying nanofriction, but the work does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Kramers Dichroism In $PT$-symmetric Magnets
authors: Oles Matsyshyn, Ying Xiong, And Justin C. W. Song
abstract:
Author(s): Oles Matsyshyn, Ying Xiong, and Justin C. W. Song

The quantum states in doubly degenerate Kramers pairs can act as an internal degree of freedom. Here, we uncover a Kramers dichroism in PT-symmetric magnets: interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light irradiation can selectively polarize Kramers partnered states allowing to control …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033046] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kramers dichroism in PT-symmetric magnets, a condensed matter phenomenon with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how circularly polarized light can selectively polarize Kramers pairs in PT-symmetric magnets, potentially enabling control of internal degrees of freedom.
method: The authors theoretically analyze interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light in PT-symmetric magnets, using symmetry arguments and band structure calculations.
result: They uncover a Kramers dichroism effect where interband transitions selectively polarize Kramers partnered states.
conclusion: This effect provides a mechanism to control Kramers pairs using light, which may have applications in spintronics or optoelectronics but is not relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Non-normal Eigenvector Amplification In Multidimensional Kesten Processes
authors: Virgile Troude And Didier Sornette
abstract:
Author(s): Virgile Troude and Didier Sornette

Heavy-tailed fluctuations and power law statistics pervade physics, finance, and economics, yet their origin is often ascribed to systems poised near criticality. Here, we show that such behavior can emerge far from instability through a universal mechanism of non-normal eigenvector amplification in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033050] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for heavy-tailed fluctuations via non-normal eigenvector amplification in multidimensional Kesten processes, far from criticality.
motivation: Heavy-tailed fluctuations are common in physics, finance, and economics, but their origin is often attributed to criticality. The authors aim to show they can emerge far from instability.
method: The authors analyze multidimensional Kesten processes and demonstrate that non-normal eigenvector amplification leads to heavy-tailed statistics without criticality.
result: They find that non-normal amplification can produce power-law distributions and large fluctuations even when the system is stable.
conclusion: Non-normal eigenvector amplification is a universal mechanism for heavy-tailed behavior, applicable across various fields.

title: Anisotropic Interactions Induce Dynamical Spin Freezing In Artificial Colloidal Ice
authors: Leonardo G. Alanis-Cantú And Antonio Ortiz-Ambriz
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo G. Alanis-Cantú and Antonio Ortiz-Ambriz

Artificial colloidal ice is an icelike system used to study the effects of frustration in controlled environments, where all degrees of freedom can be accessed at a length scale large enough for optical visualization and in real time. We modify this model system by inducing anisotropic interactions …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033051] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical spin freezing in artificial colloidal ice with anisotropic interactions, a condensed matter system not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the effects of frustration and anisotropic interactions in a controlled colloidal system, which can be visualized in real time.
method: The authors modify artificial colloidal ice by inducing anisotropic interactions and observe the resulting dynamics.
result: Anisotropic interactions lead to dynamical spin freezing, where the system gets stuck in a non-equilibrium state.
conclusion: The study provides insights into frustration and dynamics in classical spin systems, but does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ultracold Amplification Proposal For Parity Violation In Chiral Molecules
authors: Daniel Martínez-Gil, Pedro Bargueño, And Salvador Miret-Artés
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Martínez-Gil, Pedro Bargueño, and Salvador Miret-Artés

We propose a theoretical mechanism to indirectly detect the small parity-violating energy difference (PVED) between chiral enantiomers through a macroscopic enantiomeric excess observed in an ultracold gas. We consider that chiral molecules are formed resonantly via ultracold collisions of achiral d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033056] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a theoretical mechanism to detect parity violation in chiral molecules via ultracold gas amplification.
motivation: Parity-violating energy differences in chiral molecules are extremely small and have not been directly observed; the authors aim to amplify this effect to detectable levels.
method: They model ultracold collisions of achiral diatomic molecules to form chiral molecules resonantly, and analyze the resulting enantiomeric excess due to parity violation.
result: The mechanism predicts a macroscopic enantiomeric excess that could indirectly reveal the parity-violating energy difference.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a new way to detect parity violation in chiral molecules using ultracold chemistry.

title: Moiré-resonant Surface State In Ultrathin ${\mathrm{RuO}}_{2}(110)$
authors: Philipp Keßler, Andreas Feuerpfeil, Armando Consiglio, Hendrik Hohmann, Ronny Thomale, Jonas Erhardt, Bing Liu, Vedran Jovic, Ralph Claessen, Patrick Härtl, Matteo Dürrnagel, And Simon Moser
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Keßler, Andreas Feuerpfeil, Armando Consiglio, Hendrik Hohmann, Ronny Thomale, Jonas Erhardt, Bing Liu, Vedran Jovic, Ralph Claessen, Patrick Härtl, Matteo Dürrnagel, and Simon Moser

[MATH] has emerged as a prototypical candidate for altermagnetism. In the face of daunting evidence for magnetic order in the bulk, the focus naturally shifted to surfaces and ultrathin films, where Coulomb interactions are dimensionally quenched and electron correlations strongly enha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033058] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure of ultrathin RuO2(110) films, focusing on moiré-resonant surface states and altermagnetism.
motivation: RuO2 is a candidate altermagnet, but surface and thin-film properties are poorly understood; this work aims to characterize surface states and magnetic order in reduced dimensions.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations are used to probe the electronic structure of ultrathin RuO2(110) films.
result: Moiré-resonant surface states are observed, and the interplay between Coulomb interactions and magnetic order is analyzed.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into altermagnetism in thin films and highlight the role of dimensional quenching of correlations.

title: Topological States And Flat Bands In Exactly Solvable Decorated Cayley Trees
authors: Wanda P. Duss, Askar Iliasov, And Tomáš Bzdušek
abstract:
Author(s): Wanda P. Duss, Askar Iliasov, and Tomáš Bzdušek

We derive the full spectrum of decorated Cayley trees that constitute tree analogs of selected two-dimensional Euclidean lattices, namely, the Lieb, the double-Lieb, the kagome, and the star lattice. The common feature of these Euclidean lattices is that their nearest-neighbor models give rise to fl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033036] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the full spectrum of decorated Cayley trees that are tree analogs of certain two-dimensional Euclidean lattices, revealing flat bands and topological states.
motivation: To understand the spectral and topological properties of tree-like structures that mimic flat-band lattices, which are of interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors construct decorated Cayley trees corresponding to the Lieb, double-Lieb, kagome, and star lattices and exactly solve the tight-binding model using recursive techniques.
result: They obtain the complete energy spectrum, identify flat bands, and characterize topological edge states in these tree structures.
conclusion: Decorated Cayley trees provide analytically tractable models that capture key features of flat-band and topological physics, though they lack translational symmetry.

title: Topology And Geometry Of Clusters In The Vicsek Model Across Scales
authors: Ashiqur Rahman, Michael Napoli, Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Maurizio Porfiri, And Nicole Abaid
abstract:
Author(s): Ashiqur Rahman, Michael Napoli, Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Maurizio Porfiri, and Nicole Abaid

Collective motion in active matter can arise from interaction rules that generate group-level order. A seminal example is the Vicsek model, which describes flocking using a simple local alignment rule. Despite three decades of research, the network topology induced by the particles’ alignment remain…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033039] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the topology and geometry of clusters in the Vicsek model of collective motion across scales.
motivation: Understanding how local alignment rules lead to group-level order in active matter systems is a fundamental question in statistical physics.
method: The authors analyze the network topology induced by particle alignment in the Vicsek model, examining cluster properties across different scales.
result: They characterize the topological and geometric features of clusters, revealing scale-dependent behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the structure of collective motion but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Emergence Of Bistability And Even-order Harmonic Generation In A Centrosymmetric System Under Periodic Driving
authors: Fumiya Sekiguchi, Yuta Murotani, And Ryo Shimano
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Sekiguchi, Yuta Murotani, and Ryo Shimano

Nonequilibrium states of matter, when driven periodically, can exhibit exotic properties and emergent behaviors that are fundamentally distinct from those in equilibrium systems. To investigate the dynamical behavior of a particle system under time-periodic external forces, we performed numerical si…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033041] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bistability and even-order harmonic generation in a centrosymmetric system under periodic driving, focusing on non-equilibrium dynamics of a classical particle system.
motivation: To explore emergent non-equilibrium behaviors in periodically driven systems that are absent in equilibrium.
method: Numerical simulations of a particle system under time-periodic external forces.
result: Observation of bistability and even-order harmonic generation in a centrosymmetric system.
conclusion: Periodic driving can induce exotic dynamical properties in centrosymmetric systems.

title: Influence Of Excitation Energy On Microscopic Quantum Pathways For Ultrafast Charge Transfer In Van Der Waals Heterostructures
authors: Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, And Isabella Gierz
abstract:
Author(s): Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, and Isabella Gierz

Efficient charge separation in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures is crucial for optimizing light harvesting and detection applications. However, precise control over the microscopic pathways governing ultrafast charge transfer remains an open challenge. These pathways are intrinsically linked to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033033] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast charge transfer pathways in van der Waals heterostructures as a function of excitation energy.
motivation: Efficient charge separation in vdW heterostructures is crucial for light harvesting and detection, but controlling the microscopic pathways remains challenging.
method: The authors use time-resolved spectroscopy and theoretical modeling to investigate how excitation energy influences charge transfer dynamics.
result: They identify distinct microscopic pathways that depend on excitation energy, revealing mechanisms for optimizing charge separation.
conclusion: Controlling excitation energy can steer charge transfer pathways, which may improve the design of optoelectronic devices.

title: Particle-hole Origin Of Thermal Beating In Dipole-compression Modes Of A One-dimensional Bose Gas
authors: Caroline Mauron, Karen V. Kheruntsyan, And Giulia de Rosi
abstract:
Author(s): Caroline Mauron, Karen V. Kheruntsyan, and Giulia De Rosi

This work reports a beating signal of two dipole-compression collective mode frequencies evolving from the low-temperature phononic hydrodynamic regime to the collisionless limit at the hole-induced anomaly temperature. The lower (higher) frequency originates from hole (particle) spectral states, and the temperature dependence of their relative excitation strengths reflects the thermal population imbalance between particle and hole states across the anomaly temperature.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032003] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermal beating in dipole-compression modes of a 1D Bose gas, attributing it to particle-hole spectral states.
motivation: Understanding collective mode behavior in ultracold gases across temperature regimes is important for many-body physics.
method: The authors analyze the temperature dependence of two dipole-compression mode frequencies using a particle-hole picture and compare with experimental data.
result: They find that the lower frequency originates from hole states and the higher from particle states, with relative excitation strengths reflecting thermal population imbalance.
conclusion: The beating signal arises from the interplay of particle and hole excitations, providing insight into the crossover from hydrodynamic to collisionless regimes.

title: Quantum-enhanced Markov Chain Monte Carlo Sampling To Model Lagrangian Tracer Dispersion In Turbulent Boundary Layer
authors: Fabian Schindler And Jörg Schumacher
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Schindler and Jörg Schumacher

We present a quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo (QE-MCMC) method to sample turbulent acceleration vectors from a joint target distribution that depends on all three components and height to model the transport and dispersion of massless Lagrangian tracer particles in two different turbulent s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033031] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo to model Lagrangian tracer dispersion in turbulent boundary layers.
motivation: To improve sampling efficiency for high-dimensional joint distributions in turbulent flow simulations.
method: A quantum-enhanced MCMC algorithm is used to sample turbulent acceleration vectors from a joint target distribution.
result: The method demonstrates improved sampling performance for tracer dispersion in two turbulent boundary layer flows.
conclusion: Quantum-enhanced MCMC can be beneficial for computational fluid dynamics problems involving high-dimensional sampling.

title: Noiseless Limit And Improved-prior Limit Of The Maximum Entropy Method And Their Implications For The Analytic Continuation Problem
authors: Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, And Tobias Dornheim
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, and Tobias Dornheim

Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods are uniquely capable of providing exact simulations of quantum many-body systems. Unfortunately, the applications of a QMC simulation are limited because extracting dynamic properties requires solving the analytic continuation problem. Across the many fields that us…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033009] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the maximum entropy method for analytic continuation in quantum Monte Carlo simulations, focusing on its noiseless and improved-prior limits.
motivation: Extracting dynamic properties from quantum Monte Carlo simulations requires solving the analytic continuation problem, which is ill-posed and challenging.
method: The authors derive analytic expressions for the maximum entropy method in the noiseless limit and propose an improved prior to enhance reconstruction accuracy.
result: They show that in the noiseless limit, the method recovers the exact spectrum, and the improved prior reduces bias in practical applications.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insights and practical improvements for analytic continuation, benefiting quantum many-body simulations.

title: Learning Minimal Representations Of Fermionic Ground States
authors: Felix Frohnert, Emiel Koridon, And Stefano Polla
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Frohnert, Emiel Koridon, and Stefano Polla

We introduce an unsupervised machine-learning framework that discovers optimally compressed representations of quantum many-body ground states. Using an autoencoder neural network architecture on reduced density matrix data from [MATH]-site Fermi-Hubbard models, we identify minimal latent spaces with a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033014] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: An unsupervised machine learning framework using autoencoders to find minimal latent representations of fermionic ground states from reduced density matrix data.
motivation: To discover compressed representations of quantum many-body ground states that capture essential physical features, potentially aiding in understanding and simulation.
method: An autoencoder neural network is trained on reduced density matrix data from Fermi-Hubbard models to learn a minimal latent space representation.
result: The method identifies minimal latent spaces that can accurately reconstruct the original data, demonstrating compression of ground state information.
conclusion: The approach provides a data-driven way to extract minimal representations of quantum states, but its connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Markov Inequality As A Tool For Linear-scaling Estimation Of Local Observables
authors: H. P. Veiga, D. R. Pinheiro, J. P. Santos Pires, And J. M. Viana Parente Lopes
abstract:
Author(s): H. P. Veiga, D. R. Pinheiro, J. P. Santos Pires, and J. M. Viana Parente Lopes

We introduce a linear-scaling stochastic method to compute real-space maps of any positive local spectral operator in a tight-binding model. By employing positive semidefinite estimators, the sampling error at each site can be rigorously bounded relative to the mean via the Markov inequality, overco…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033015] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A linear-scaling stochastic method for computing local spectral operators in tight-binding models using Markov inequality to bound sampling error.
motivation: To efficiently compute real-space maps of local observables in large tight-binding systems without full diagonalization.
method: Uses positive semidefinite estimators and Markov inequality to bound sampling error per site, achieving linear scaling with system size.
result: The method provides rigorous error bounds and linear-scaling computational cost, demonstrated on graphene and other tight-binding models.
conclusion: The approach enables efficient and accurate estimation of local spectral properties in large quantum systems.

title: Aging Of Ring Polymeric Topological Glass Formers Via Thermal Quench
authors: Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, And Satyavani Vemparala
abstract:
Author(s): Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, and Satyavani Vemparala

We investigate the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of dense, topologically constrained ring-polymer systems subjected to instantaneous thermal quenches, using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. We show that the onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with incre…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033019] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of ring-polymer systems after thermal quench using molecular dynamics simulations.
motivation: To understand how topological constraints and polymer stiffness affect dynamical arrest in ring-polymer glasses.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of dense ring-polymer systems subjected to instantaneous thermal quenches.
result: The onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with increasing stiffness leading to slower dynamics.
conclusion: Ring-polymer topology and stiffness play key roles in glass formation, but the work is focused on polymer physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Electric-Field Control Of Interlayer Binding And Friction In $h$-BN Contacts
authors: Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, And Oded Hod
abstract:
Author(s): Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, and Oded Hod

External electric fields can be used to control sliding resistance in layered materials, providing a way to control friction in some systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field control of interlayer binding and friction in h-BN contacts, a topic in nanoscale tribology.
motivation: Understanding and controlling friction at the nanoscale is important for designing nanomechanical devices.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the effect of external electric fields on interlayer interactions and sliding resistance.
result: They find that electric fields can significantly modulate interlayer binding and friction, offering a potential mechanism for active friction control.
conclusion: Electric fields provide a viable route to control friction in layered materials like h-BN, which may have applications in nanoscale devices.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Nägele and Florian Marquardt

ꜱᴄɪᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇʀ, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, automates the process of scientific research and discovery and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031002] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an AI agent that automates scientific discovery by exploring physics models, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: To automate the process of scientific research and discovery in physics using large language models.
method: The authors develop SciExplorer, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, which autonomously explores and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.
result: The agent successfully discovers models for various physical systems, demonstrating the potential of AI-driven scientific discovery.
conclusion: LLM-based agents can automate parts of the scientific discovery process, but the paper is not focused on quantum information theory or related fields.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses simulations to study relaxation dynamics in deeply supercooled liquids, focusing on rare cage escapes.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in glass-forming liquids is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare events.
result: The authors identify that rare cage escapes are the primary drivers of relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes.
motivation: Previous complexity proofs for BosonSampling only applied to the dilute regime, but experimental demonstrations operate in the saturated regime; bridging this gap is necessary to validate quantum advantage claims.
method: The authors develop new computational complexity arguments, likely involving approximate average-case hardness and anticoncentration, adapted to the saturated regime where the number of photons scales linearly with modes.
result: They prove that BosonSampling in the saturated regime remains classically hard under plausible conjectures, extending the theoretical basis for quantum advantage experiments.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous complexity-theoretic support for current photonic quantum advantage experiments, confirming that they are indeed hard to simulate classically.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum chiral solitons in spin chains and their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, with detection via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the dynamics and quantization of chiral solitons in magnetic systems, which are topological excitations in spin chains.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed for chiral solitons, and their low-energy properties are analyzed using field theory techniques.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase, detectable by inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical description of chiral soliton dynamics and suggests experimental signatures in neutron scattering experiments.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of three-dimensional conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative discretization of the sphere, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs, and analyze the spectrum and correlation functions.
result: They find evidence of emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute critical exponents.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying strongly coupled CFTs, and emergent supersymmetry may be a generic feature of certain fermionic CFTs.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin textures in moiré materials is important for potential information manipulation, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures and identify magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2, establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for studying spin moiré physics but does not directly contribute to quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological Dirac magnons in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature, focusing on the stability of magnon gaps near the Curie point.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of topological magnon gaps at finite temperatures is crucial for designing spintronic devices, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the behavior of topological magnon gaps as temperature approaches the Curie point.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie temperature.
conclusion: The stability of topological magnon gaps provides a roadmap for robust spintronic devices, but the work is purely condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics relevance.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: To predict physical links in networks where direct observation is difficult.
method: Uses a physics-informed approach combining network science and dynamical systems theory.
result: The framework successfully infers causal links across a range of networked dynamics.
conclusion: The method provides a general tool for link prediction in complex networks.

Local protonic gating in

tldr: This paper demonstrates a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect in gate-defined homojunctions using local protonic gating.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers via topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or numerical methods.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: The work offers a robust mechanism for engineering anyonic exciton superfluids in quantum Hall bilayers.

authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the three-dimensional XY universality class and nonlinear magnetic susceptibility in a kagome ice compound HoAgGe, revealing hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To understand the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which exhibits a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.

result: The measurements reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
conclusion: The study provides evidence for a novel ground state in kagome ice compounds, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but many such bands are only stable at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a material platform with intrinsic flat bands that persist at room temperature.
method: The authors synthesized layered transition-metal oxyhalides and performed angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to map the electronic band structure, revealing flat bands that are orbital-selective and robust up to room temperature.
result: They observed intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, with orbital selectivity, providing a tunable platform for studying strongly correlated electron states.
conclusion: These materials offer a promising platform for exploring flat-band physics and strongly correlated phenomena at ambient conditions, potentially enabling new quantum devices.

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe

motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material, using optical spectroscopy.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the unusual critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which suppress density fluctuations yet exhibit high susceptibility at the liquid-vapor critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and possibly simulations to analyze the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show suppressed fluctuations but enhanced susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The work reveals a new class of critical behavior in hyperuniform fluids, relevant to soft matter physics but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between different ferroic orders (polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational) in a single material, which is of interest for fundamental condensed matter physics.

result: The study identifies a uniform ferro-rotational state that couples polarity and chirality, leading to complex mixed-type domain walls.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis to characterize the scattering behavior.
result: Residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of full transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and suggest design modifications.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
