tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured framework with five stages, each with specific milestones, based on their expertise in quantum algorithms and hardware.
result: A five-stage roadmap for quantum computing utility is presented, but no new technical results or experiments are reported.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level guide for the field but does not contain novel technical contributions.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnets, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights the rapid progress in understanding magnetic phenomena in 2D materials and their potential for applications.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to unify dynamical evolution via space-time duality.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on lattice systems, treating space and time on the same footing, leads to solvable models using brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of the space-time duality approach and its relationship with quantum computation, but does not present new results.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a unified view of quantum many-body dynamics, but the paper is a review without novel contributions.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from the kagome lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing electronic structure and many-body effects.
result: Identifies key phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and sublattice interference effects.
conclusion: Kagome metals provide a platform for realizing novel electronic states driven by frustration and interference.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex systems, but a unified field-theoretic framework is lacking.
method: The authors review and unify various field-theoretic approaches (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: They demonstrate how these methods can be applied to chemical systems and extended to ecology and epidemiology.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful and unifying framework for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the Universe, and their properties provide crucial information about matter under extreme compression.
method: The review summarizes constraints from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: Recent observations have improved constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, but the equation of state at supranuclear densities remains uncertain.
conclusion: Future observations, especially from gravitational-wave detectors and X-ray telescopes, will further refine our understanding of dense matter.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key advances and open questions in spin-glass dynamics.
conclusion: Spin-glass research continues to benefit from interdisciplinary approaches, with future opportunities in both fundamental and applied contexts.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological phenomena observed.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with many open questions, and the review serves as a guide for future research.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications like photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models describing internal conversion, including nonradiative mechanisms and their incorporation into application-oriented studies.
result: The review summarizes the current state of theoretical methods for internal conversion and provides an outlook for future research directions.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are well-developed but need further integration into practical applications in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for future spintronic devices, and understanding their quantum aspects is crucial for advancing both fundamental physics and applications.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum features, and interactions, synthesizing results from condensed matter physics.
result: It highlights quantum-mechanical effects in skyrmion dynamics, such as quantum tunneling and entanglement, and discusses their potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that could be harnessed for novel technologies, but the field is still developing and many open questions remain.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe discrete fundamental symmetries, the paper surveys spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques.
result: The review compiles current theoretical predictions and experimental constraints on spin-dependent exotic interactions mediated by exotic bosons.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential connections to dark matter and dark energy, but no definitive evidence has been found.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental limits, but some measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to novel materials.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of circumstances where measured properties exceed classical bounds and identifies which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, homogeneity) are violated.
result: It shows that apparent violations arise from measurement conditions that violate assumptions, and that materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
conclusion: The findings clarify the limits of classical thermodynamic bounds and provide a framework for developing materials with extreme properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing nonstandard geometries in synthetic quantum matter.
result: Summarizes progress in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional simulations across platforms.
conclusion: These synthetic systems offer new avenues for studying quantum many-body physics in geometries not naturally available.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, exploring whether gravity induces decoherence or entanglement.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theories of gravity-induced decoherence and collapse, and experiments testing gravity-mediated entanglement between massive particles.
result: Ongoing experiments aim to determine whether gravity causes decoherence or can mediate entanglement, guiding future theoretical descriptions.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems serve as interfaces to probe quantum gravity effects, but conclusive results are pending.

title: Optical Soliton Cooper Pairs In Mamyshev Oscillators
authors: Chenxiao Hao, Tianhao Xian, Zhenghu Chang, Yahan Du, And Li Zhan
abstract:
Author(s): Chenxiao Hao, Tianhao Xian, Zhenghu Chang, Yahan Du, and Li Zhan

The framework of superconductivity unveiled the striking concept that electrons form Cooper pairs through the subtle interplay of lattice vibrations, surmounting their Coulombic repulsion in the process. The concept of Cooper pairs has been established beyond the Fermi system, and this pairing mecha…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033801] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an optical analog of Cooper pairs using soliton interactions in Mamyshev oscillators.
motivation: To explore the concept of Cooper pairing beyond condensed matter systems and demonstrate it in a classical optical system.
method: The authors theoretically model and experimentally demonstrate soliton bound states in a Mamyshev oscillator, drawing an analogy to Cooper pair formation.
result: They observe stable soliton pairs that exhibit binding energy and pairing behavior analogous to Cooper pairs.
conclusion: The work provides a classical optical analogue of Cooper pairing, potentially inspiring new insights into nonlinear wave interactions.

title: Pushy Random Walk: A Minimal Model For Transport In Deformable Media
authors: Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Itamar Shitrit, Shlomi Reuveni, And Sidney Redner
abstract:
Author(s): Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Itamar Shitrit, Shlomi Reuveni, and Sidney Redner

In a minimal model of a pushy random walk, a moving tracer can displace obstacles, giving rise to new diffusive behaviors in both 1D and 2D.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 037101] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: A minimal model of a pushy random walk where a tracer displaces obstacles, leading to new diffusive behaviors in 1D and 2D.
motivation: To understand transport in deformable media, such as biological or soft matter systems, where moving objects can alter the environment.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a random walk model where the tracer pushes obstacles aside, modifying the medium.
result: The model exhibits anomalous diffusion and non-Gaussian statistics, with distinct regimes in 1D and 2D.
conclusion: The pushy random walk provides a minimal framework for transport in deformable media, with potential applications in biophysics and materials science.

title: Vibrational-Entropy-Driven Compensation Mechanism On The Rutile ${\mathrm{TiO}}_{2}\text{ }(111)$ Polar Surface
authors: Fangwen Yang, Kai Zhang, Chen Zou, Ying Jiang, Zhong-Kang Han, Wentao Yuan, And Yong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Fangwen Yang, Kai Zhang, Chen Zou, Ying Jiang, Zhong-Kang Han, Wentao Yuan, and Yong Wang

Polar surfaces, known for their unique electronic and chemical properties, play vital roles in catalysis and electronics, yet their atomic structures remain difficult to resolve due to intrinsic instability often mitigated by surface reconstruction. However, the role of entropy, particularly vibrati…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026201] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the atomic structure and vibrational entropy-driven compensation mechanism of a polar surface of rutile TiO2.
motivation: Polar surfaces are important in catalysis and electronics but their atomic structures are difficult to resolve due to instability; understanding entropy's role in stabilization is key.
method: The authors combine first-principles calculations and experimental techniques to investigate the surface reconstruction and vibrational entropy contributions.
result: They identify a vibrational-entropy-driven compensation mechanism that stabilizes the polar surface.
conclusion: Vibrational entropy plays a crucial role in the stability of polar surfaces, which has implications for surface science and materials design.

title: Quantum Theory Of Photon Emission During Strong-laser-field-induced Ionization. Ii. Continuum Dynamics
authors: D. B. Milošević And W. Becker
abstract:
Author(s): D. B. Milošević and W. Becker

Emission of a photon during the process of above-threshold ionization is investigated. In previous work [D. B. Milošević,
tldr: This paper studies photon emission during strong-laser-field-induced ionization using the strong-field approximation.
motivation: To understand the continuum dynamics of electrons in strong laser fields and the associated photon emission process.
method: The authors extend previous work by including higher-order terms in the strong-field approximation for the matrix element describing direct and rescattering ionization channels.
result: They derive expressions for the photon emission probability and analyze its dependence on laser parameters and electron trajectories.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed theoretical description of photon emission during ionization, but it is focused on atomic physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Revealing Hidden Topology Of Complex Vector Beams Via Plasmonic Interactions
authors: Sahil Sahoo, Ahmed Lafeef Ettapuram Naduvilepurayil, Andre Yaroshevsky, Peter Banzer, And Yuri Gorodetski
abstract:
Author(s): Sahil Sahoo, Ahmed Lafeef Ettapuram Naduvilepurayil, Andre Yaroshevsky, Peter Banzer, and Yuri Gorodetski

Structured light beams with space-variant polarization can be efficiently generated using a voltage-tunable nematic liquid crystal ([MATH] plate). By appropriately selecting the input state and the retardation of the [MATH] plate, an optical field acquires a spatially structured polarization distribution …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013514] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the topological properties of complex vector beams revealed through plasmonic interactions.
motivation: To understand and characterize hidden topological features of structured light beams using plasmonic nanostructures.
method: Experimental generation of vector beams with a liquid crystal q-plate and probing their polarization structure via plasmonic interactions.
result: Plasmonic interactions reveal topological features of vector beams that are not apparent in free-space propagation.
conclusion: Plasmonic interactions provide a sensitive probe for the topology of complex vector beams, with potential applications in optical manipulation and sensing.

title: Strain-tunable Optical Responses And Topological Phase Transitions In The Two-dimensional Altermagnet Vo
authors: Meijun Wang, Ying Liu, Yefeng Li, Yong-An Zhong, Lei Jin, Xuefang Dai, Guodong Liu, And Xiaoming Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Meijun Wang, Ying Liu, Yefeng Li, Yong-An Zhong, Lei Jin, Xuefang Dai, Guodong Liu, and Xiaoming Zhang

Two-dimensional altermagnets (AMs) with tunable electronic and topological properties offer promising opportunities for next-generation spintronic and optoelectronic applications. Here, we predict that monolayer VO (ML-VO) is a two-dimensional AM semiconductor with collinear magnetic ordering and $d…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014417] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts monolayer VO as a two-dimensional altermagnet semiconductor with strain-tunable optical and topological properties.
motivation: To explore two-dimensional altermagnets with tunable electronic and topological properties for spintronic and optoelectronic applications.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory to study electronic structure, optical responses, and topological phase transitions under strain.
result: Monolayer VO is a 2D altermagnet semiconductor; strain induces topological phase transitions and modifies optical properties.
conclusion: ML-VO is a promising platform for strain-tunable spintronic and optoelectronic devices.

title: Ultrafast Nonthermal Suppression Of Ferroelectricity By Carrier Screening In ${\mathrm{LiNbO}}_{3}$
authors: Man Tou Wong, Zhuquan Zhang, Zi-Jie Liu, And Keith A. Nelson
abstract:
Author(s): Man Tou Wong, Zhuquan Zhang, Zi-Jie Liu, and Keith A. Nelson

Ferroelectric materials are key to energy-efficient electronics, memory, and optical applications. While charge carriers typically screen and suppress ferroelectricity, their role under nonequilibrium conditions remains elusive. Here, we use femtosecond laser pulses to liberate trapped carriers in $…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034309] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast suppression of ferroelectricity in LiNbO3 via carrier screening using femtosecond laser pulses.
motivation: Understanding nonequilibrium carrier screening effects in ferroelectrics is important for energy-efficient electronics and memory applications.
method: Femtosecond laser pulses are used to liberate trapped carriers, and the resulting suppression of ferroelectricity is probed.
result: The experiments demonstrate nonthermal suppression of ferroelectric order due to carrier screening on ultrafast timescales.
conclusion: Carrier screening can rapidly and nonthermally suppress ferroelectricity, offering a new mechanism for ultrafast control of ferroelectric materials.

title: Single-crystal Growth And Magnetic, Magnetoelectric, And Optical Properties Of Ferroaxial-type ${\mathrm{SrMn}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{6}{\mathrm{Te}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{18}$
authors: Ryoya Nakamura, Shinichiro Asai, Yusuke Nambu, Takatsugu Masuda, And Kenta Kimura
abstract:
Author(s): Ryoya Nakamura, Shinichiro Asai, Yusuke Nambu, Takatsugu Masuda, and Kenta Kimura

Single crystals of [MATH], a member of the ferroaxial-type magnetic oxide family [MATH] ([MATH], Sr; [MATH], Cd; [MATH], Co), have been successfully grow…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034415] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the growth and characterization of single-crystal SrMn2Ni6Te3O18, focusing on its magnetic, magnetoelectric, and optical properties.
motivation: To explore the ferroaxial-type magnetic oxide family and understand the interplay between magnetism, ferroelectricity, and optical properties in these materials.
method: Single crystals were grown, and measurements of magnetization, magnetoelectric effect, and optical spectroscopy were performed.
result: The material exhibits specific magnetic ordering, magnetoelectric coupling, and optical absorption features.
conclusion: The study provides a comprehensive characterization of a new ferroaxial compound, contributing to the understanding of multiferroic materials.

title: Random Walks On Disordered Lattices: The Role Of Effective Porosity, Blocked Domain Width, And Spatial Correlations
authors: Nathann Teixeira Rodrigues And Fábio D. A. Aarão Reis
abstract:
Author(s): Nathann Teixeira Rodrigues and Fábio D. A. Aarão Reis

We perform a numerical study of random walks (RWs) on 3D lattices with random and periodic distributions of blocked sites, analyze the dependence of effective diffusion coefficients [MATH] on the effective porosity [MATH], and show applications to diffusive solute transport in some porous materials.…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014122] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of random walks on disordered 3D lattices, focusing on effective diffusion coefficients and their dependence on porosity and spatial correlations.
motivation: To understand how disorder and spatial correlations affect diffusion in porous materials, which is relevant for solute transport applications.
method: Monte Carlo simulations of random walks on 3D lattices with random and periodic distributions of blocked sites, measuring mean squared displacement and effective diffusion coefficients.
result: Effective diffusion coefficients depend on effective porosity and blocked domain width; spatial correlations can enhance or hinder diffusion depending on the arrangement.
conclusion: The study provides insights into transport in disordered media but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Alternating Pattern Formation In Oscillatory Media With Spatially Uniform And Nonuniform Global Feedback
authors: Zhilin Qu, Chunli Huang, And Fengze Sui
abstract:
Author(s): Zhilin Qu, Chunli Huang, and Fengze Sui

Alternating (temporally period-2) stripes, clusters, and labyrinths have been observed in chemical and biochemical reactions, in Min-protein dynamics in E. coli and in vitro systems, and in calcium alternans in cardiac myocytes. However, the mechanisms underlying the formation of these spatiotempora…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014211] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies alternating pattern formation in oscillatory media with global feedback, focusing on chemical and biological systems.
motivation: Understanding mechanisms behind alternating stripes, clusters, and labyrinths observed in chemical reactions and biological systems like Min-protein dynamics and cardiac alternans.
method: The authors analyze a generic model of oscillatory media with spatially uniform and nonuniform global feedback, using theoretical and computational approaches.
result: They identify conditions and mechanisms leading to alternating pattern formation, showing how global feedback can induce period-2 spatiotemporal patterns.
conclusion: The work provides insights into pattern formation in oscillatory media, relevant to chemical and biological contexts, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Unified Ott-Antonsen Framework For Stability And Bifurcations In Ring Swarmalators
authors: Can Xu, Wenhan Xu, And Xingang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Can Xu, Wenhan Xu, and Xingang Wang

Swarmalators, a prototypical model that integrates temporal rhythms with spatial swarming, have been widely used to explore the collective dynamics observed in active-matter systems. Although numerical simulations have revealed a variety of collective states, a general theoretical framework for the …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014212] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unified theoretical framework for analyzing stability and bifurcations in ring swarmalator systems, which combine synchronization and swarming.
motivation: Swarmalators are important for understanding collective dynamics in active matter, but a general theoretical framework for their stability and bifurcations was lacking.
method: The authors extend the Ott-Antonsen ansatz to ring swarmalator models, deriving reduced equations for the macroscopic order parameters and analyzing their stability and bifurcations.
result: They obtain analytical conditions for the onset of various collective states, including phase-locked, wave, and incoherent states, and validate them with numerical simulations.
conclusion: The unified framework provides a powerful tool for studying swarmalator dynamics and can be extended to other coupled oscillator-swarm systems.

title: Intrinsic Density Of States And The Origin Of Gamma Volume Distributions In Jammed Granular Matter
authors: Ching Chang, Yang Chang, And Jason Chao
abstract:
Author(s): Ching Chang, Yang Chang, and Jason Chao

Athermal systems such as granular materials exhibit reproducible volume fluctuations despite the absence of thermal equilibration, yet a quantitative statistical-mechanical description remains incomplete. Within the Edwards ensemble, volume replaces energy as the conserved quantity and compactivity …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015410] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies volume fluctuations in jammed granular matter using the Edwards ensemble, a statistical mechanics approach for athermal systems.
motivation: Granular materials exhibit reproducible volume fluctuations without thermal equilibration, and a quantitative statistical-mechanical description is needed.
method: The authors apply the Edwards ensemble, where volume replaces energy as the conserved quantity, and analyze the intrinsic density of states to explain gamma volume distributions.
result: The intrinsic density of states derived from the Edwards ensemble reproduces the observed gamma volume distributions in jammed granular matter.
conclusion: The Edwards ensemble provides a valid statistical-mechanical framework for describing volume fluctuations in athermal granular systems.

title: Hamiltonian Active Particles In Incompressible Fluid Membranes
authors: Sneha Krishnan And Rickmoy Samanta
abstract:
Author(s): Sneha Krishnan and Rickmoy Samanta

Active proteins and membrane-bound motors exert force dipole flows along fluid interfaces and lipid bilayers. We develop a Hamiltonian framework for the interactions of pusher and puller dipoles embedded in an incompressible two-dimensional membrane supported by a shallow viscous subphase. Beginning…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015102] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a Hamiltonian framework for active particles in fluid membranes, focusing on hydrodynamic interactions of force dipoles.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of active proteins and membrane-bound motors in biological membranes, which are often modeled as incompressible fluids.
method: The authors construct a Hamiltonian formalism for pusher and puller dipoles embedded in a 2D incompressible membrane supported by a shallow viscous subphase, deriving equations of motion from the Hamiltonian.
result: The framework captures the interactions between active dipoles and the resulting flow fields in the membrane.
conclusion: The Hamiltonian approach provides a systematic way to study active particle dynamics in fluid membranes, with potential applications to biological systems.

title: Model-free Analysis Of Complex Systems Using Delayed-feedback Echo State Network
authors: Wenjing Guo, Shuang Li, Jianming Liu, Eric Li, And Xu Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenjing Guo, Shuang Li, Jianming Liu, Eric Li, and Xu Xu

Investigating the dynamical behavior of complex systems from data poses formidable challenges in the field of nonlinear science. This paper proposes a delayed-feedback echo state network ( df-ESN) model specifically designed for modeling and analyzing complex systems from data. The df-ESN introdu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014204] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a delayed-feedback echo state network for model-free analysis of complex systems from data.
motivation: Investigating dynamical behavior of complex systems from data is challenging; existing methods may not capture long-term dependencies.
method: The authors introduce a delayed-feedback echo state network (df-ESN) that incorporates delayed connections to improve modeling of complex dynamics.
result: The df-ESN demonstrates improved performance in modeling and analyzing complex systems compared to standard echo state networks.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical tool for data-driven analysis of complex systems, but does not contribute to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Distinct Phenomenon On Chaos Synchrony: Chirality
authors: Gualberto C. Solís-Perales And Ricardo Femat
abstract:
Author(s): Gualberto C. Solís-Perales and Ricardo Femat

Among others, chirality is a property of organometallic molecules whose main feature is that the spatial superposition is exclusively observed through a specular plane. A specular plane is a physical kind of subspace onto which chiral objects can already be superposed. That is, chirality corresponds…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014206] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies chirality in the context of chaos synchrony, a topic unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Chirality is a property of molecules where spatial superposition is only observable through a specular plane; the authors aim to explore this phenomenon in chaotic synchronization.
method: The paper likely uses dynamical systems theory and numerical simulations to analyze chirality in coupled chaotic oscillators.
result: The paper reports a distinct phenomenon of chirality in chaos synchrony, but no specific results are provided in the abstract.
conclusion: The work contributes to the understanding of chirality in nonlinear dynamics, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Structural And Thermal Confinement Of Schwarz Crystals
authors: Dan Huang, Huangliu Fu, Meng Lyu, Yuanwen Feng, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Takashi Honda, Enke Liu, Bing Li, Xiuyan Li, And Ke Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Dan Huang, Huangliu Fu, Meng Lyu, Yuanwen Feng, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Takashi Honda, Enke Liu, Bing Li, Xiuyan Li, and Ke Lu

As a nontrivial state of solid, Schwarz crystal manifests itself in extremely refined nanograins and triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) grain boundaries, and therefore exceptional thermal and mechanical stability. However, it remains unexploited how the structural units interact and thermal tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033017] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Schwarz crystals, a nanostructured solid with triply periodic minimal surface grain boundaries, focusing on their structural and thermal properties.
motivation: To understand how structural units interact and thermal transport occurs in Schwarz crystals, which exhibit exceptional stability.
method: Experimental characterization using neutron scattering and other techniques to probe structural and thermal confinement effects.
result: The paper reveals how the unique grain boundary structure influences thermal properties.
conclusion: Schwarz crystals have potential for applications requiring high thermal and mechanical stability, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning theory.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for training stability and performance, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks and analyze training instabilities.
result: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical explanation for abrupt learning and identifies ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The work contributes to machine learning theory but is outside the scope of quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can be used as cryptographic primitives by analyzing their collision resistance.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, likely using theoretical complexity arguments and algorithmic analysis.
result: Efficient algorithms fail to find collisions in the neural network, suggesting potential for cryptographic applications.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the description of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on momentum and spin densities.
motivation: Understanding how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles is fundamental for applications like optical trapping and acoustic manipulation.
method: The authors present a theoretical framework based on local energy, momentum, and spin densities in classical wave fields, covering both optics and acoustics.
result: They show that the same physical principles govern forces and torques in both optical and acoustic systems, enabling a unified description.
conclusion: This unified perspective can guide the design of advanced particle manipulation techniques using light and sound.

title: Hidden Density-Wave Instability In The Trimer Ruthenate ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{4}{\mathrm{Ru}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{10}$
authors: Gang Cao, Hengdi Zhao, Adrienne Bond, Tristan R. Cao, Gabriel Schebel, Arabella Quane, Yifei Ni, Yu Zhang, Logan Wall, Rahul Nandkishore, Pedro Schlottmann, Stephan Rosenkranz, And Feng Ye
abstract:
Author(s): Gang Cao, Hengdi Zhao, Adrienne Bond, Tristan R. Cao, Gabriel Schebel, Arabella Quane, Yifei Ni, Yu Zhang, Logan Wall, Rahul Nandkishore, Pedro Schlottmann, Stephan Rosenkranz, and Feng Ye

Simultaneous signatures in structure, thermodynamics, and transport reveal a strongly pinned density-wave in an antiferromagnetic oxide previously regarded as a purely magnetic insulator.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036502] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of a hidden density-wave instability in a trimer ruthenate, previously considered a purely magnetic insulator.
motivation: To understand the interplay between structure, thermodynamics, and transport in antiferromagnetic oxides, and to reveal hidden electronic instabilities.
method: Combined structural, thermodynamic, and transport measurements on Ba4Ru3O10 single crystals.
result: Simultaneous signatures in structure, thermodynamics, and transport indicate a strongly pinned density-wave order.
conclusion: The material exhibits a hidden density-wave instability beyond its known magnetic properties.

title: Accelerated Sequential Posterior Inference Via Reuse For Gravitational-Wave Analyses
authors: Michael J. Williams
abstract:
Author(s): Michael J. Williams

We introduce accelerated sequential posterior inference via reuse (ASPIRE), a broadly applicable framework that transforms existing posterior samples and Bayesian evidence estimates into unbiased results under alternative models without rerunning the original analysis. ASPIRE combines normalizing fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021410] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a framework for accelerating sequential posterior inference in gravitational-wave analyses using normalizing flows.
motivation: Gravitational-wave parameter estimation is computationally expensive, and re-running analyses for alternative models is inefficient.
method: ASPIRE transforms existing posterior samples and Bayesian evidence estimates into unbiased results under alternative models without rerunning the original analysis, using normalizing flows.
result: The method achieves significant computational speedups while maintaining unbiasedness.
conclusion: ASPIRE provides a broadly applicable framework for efficient Bayesian inference in gravitational-wave astronomy.

title: Extended Haloscope Search And Exclusion Of A Candidate Signal Near 1.036 GHz
authors: Saebyeok Ahn et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Saebyeok Ahn et al.

We report a follow-up axion haloscope search near 1.036 GHz that completes and extends our previous work [Ahn et al.
tldr: This paper reports an extended axion haloscope search near 1.036 GHz, excluding a candidate signal.
motivation: To follow up on a previous axion search where part of the data could not be analyzed due to unrecorded experimental information, and to extend the search.
method: The authors used a haloscope setup with HEMT-based readout to search for axion dark matter in the microwave frequency range.
result: No axion signal was found, and the candidate signal from the previous work was excluded.
conclusion: The null result sets new constraints on axion parameters in the searched mass range.

title: Cavendish Tests Of Millicharged Particles
authors: Asher Berlin, Zachary Bogorad, Peter W. Graham, And Harikrishnan Ramani
abstract:
Author(s): Asher Berlin, Zachary Bogorad, Peter W. Graham, and Harikrishnan Ramani

Decades-old experiments have now been enlisted to set new bounds on the properties of a hypothetical particle that bears a tiny fraction of the electron’s charge.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021804] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses historical Cavendish experiments to set new bounds on millicharged particles.
motivation: Millicharged particles are a hypothetical dark sector candidate; existing experimental bounds can be improved by reanalyzing old data.
method: The authors reinterpret data from Cavendish-type torsion balance experiments to constrain the force between millicharged particles and neutral matter.
result: New, stronger limits are placed on the charge and mass of millicharged particles.
conclusion: Old experiments remain valuable for probing new physics, and the bounds set are competitive with dedicated searches.

title: Positron Annihilation In Multiprincipal Element Alloys For The Identification Of Chemical Short-Range-Order Structures
authors: Qigui Yang, Qianqian Wang, Yao Yu, Te Zhu, Peng Zhang, Ping Wang, Yiping Lu, And Xingzhong Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Qigui Yang, Qianqian Wang, Yao Yu, Te Zhu, Peng Zhang, Ping Wang, Yiping Lu, and Xingzhong Cao

Chemical short-range order (SRO) is an intrinsic feature of the atomic structures in multiprincipal element alloys (MPEAs). Effective control of SRO structures could considerably improve the strength and ductility of MPEAs. However, the experimental characterization of SRO remains highly challenging…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026101] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses positron annihilation spectroscopy to characterize chemical short-range order in multiprincipal element alloys.
motivation: Chemical short-range order (SRO) is crucial for improving mechanical properties of multiprincipal element alloys, but experimental characterization is challenging.
method: Positron annihilation spectroscopy is employed to probe atomic-scale defects and local electron density changes associated with SRO structures.
result: The technique successfully identifies different SRO structures in the alloys, demonstrating sensitivity to local chemical ordering.
conclusion: Positron annihilation spectroscopy is a viable tool for SRO characterization, aiding in the design of high-performance alloys.

title: Gain-controlled Directional Scattering In Core-shell Nanoparticles Mediated By Magnetic Toroidal Dipoles
authors: Tiago José Arruda
abstract:
Author(s): Tiago José Arruda

Controlling how nanostructures scatter light usually depends on rigid material geometries, but adding optical gain to a core-shell nanoparticle allows researchers to actively flip the direction of light on demand. By selectively tuning the phase of magnetic toroidal dipoles, this study demonstrates a continuous mechanism to steer radiation from suppressed backscattering to suppressed forward scattering.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L011502] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates active control of directional light scattering in core-shell nanoparticles by tuning magnetic toroidal dipoles via optical gain.
motivation: To achieve dynamic control over light scattering direction without relying on rigid material geometries.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a core-shell nanoparticle with optical gain, showing that the phase of magnetic toroidal dipoles can be tuned to switch between suppressed backscattering and suppressed forward scattering.
result: A continuous mechanism to steer radiation direction is demonstrated, mediated by magnetic toroidal dipole phase control.
conclusion: Optical gain in core-shell nanoparticles enables active, reversible control of scattering direction, with potential applications in nanophotonics.

title: Weak Decay Of The Positronium Ion
authors: Nishat Ul Sani, Muhammad Jamil Aslam, And Ishtiaq Ahmed
abstract:
Author(s): Nishat Ul Sani, Muhammad Jamil Aslam, and Ishtiaq Ahmed

The positronium ion [MATH], a Coulombic three-body bound state of two electrons and a positron, predominantly decays via electron-positron annihilation into electromagnetic final states. While its radiative decay channels have been extensively studied, much less attention has been giv…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012807] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the weak decay of the positronium ion, a three-body bound state, which is a topic in particle physics.
motivation: The weak decay channels of the positronium ion have received little attention compared to its radiative decays, and understanding them could provide insights into fundamental interactions.
method: The authors perform theoretical calculations of the weak decay rates using quantum electrodynamics and weak interaction theory.
result: They compute the branching ratios for various weak decay modes of the positronium ion.
conclusion: The weak decay of the positronium ion is found to be extremely rare, but potentially observable in future experiments.

title: Dynamics Of Relativistic Vortex Electrons In An Obliquely Incident Laser Beam
authors: Zhi-Heng Tang, Wei-Min Wang, Guo-Qian Liao, And Yu-Tong Li
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Heng Tang, Wei-Min Wang, Guo-Qian Liao, and Yu-Tong Li

The dynamics of relativistic vortex electrons in laser fields is typically studied under the assumption of normal laser incidence, a configuration that preserves the transverse topological structure. In practical experiments, however, perfectly normal incidence is hard to achieve and oblique inciden…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013108] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of relativistic vortex electrons in an obliquely incident laser beam, focusing on the effects of oblique incidence on the electron's orbital angular momentum and trajectory.
motivation: Understanding the behavior of vortex electrons in realistic experimental conditions where perfect normal incidence is not achievable.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and numerical simulations to model the interaction of relativistic vortex electrons with an obliquely incident laser beam.
result: Oblique incidence leads to a reduction in the electron's orbital angular momentum and alters its trajectory compared to normal incidence.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of considering oblique incidence in experiments involving vortex electrons and laser fields.

title: Pressure-induced Structural Transitions And Dome-shaped Superconductivity In The Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{PbBi}}_{6}{\mathrm{Te}}_{10}$
authors: Junying Hu, Guangyang Dai, Liang Ma, Jingkai Bi, Jianyong Chen, And Zhiwei Men
abstract:
Author(s): JunYing Hu, GuangYang Dai, Liang Ma, JingKai Bi, JianYong Chen, and ZhiWei Men

Topological insulators (TIs) constitute a unique class of quantum materials owing to their topology-protected electron states. While pressure is an effective way to induce superconductivity in TIs, superconductivity often appears after phase transition or structural disorder. Therefore, identifying …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024103] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pressure-induced structural transitions and superconductivity in the topological insulator PbBi6Te10.
motivation: Topological insulators can become superconducting under pressure, but the relationship between structural changes and superconductivity is not well understood.
method: The authors perform high-pressure experiments and characterize structural and superconducting properties using X-ray diffraction and electrical transport measurements.
result: They observe a dome-shaped superconducting phase and identify structural transitions that correlate with the superconducting behavior.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the interplay between structural disorder and superconductivity in topological insulators.

title: Local Electronic Structure And Dynamics Of Hydrogen In ${\mathrm{CeO}}_{2}$
authors: A. Koda, T. U. Ito, M. Hiraishi, H. Okabe, And R. Kadono
abstract:
Author(s): A. Koda, T. U. Ito, M. Hiraishi, H. Okabe, and R. Kadono

The local electronic states of muon (Mu) as an isotope of hydrogen (H) in high-quality single-crystalline ceria ([MATH]) are investigated using muon spin rotation/relaxation and first-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Upon positive muon implantation, both paramag…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020101] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the local electronic structure and dynamics of hydrogen in CeO2 using muon spin rotation and DFT calculations.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen behavior in ceria is important for applications in catalysis and solid oxide fuel cells, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Muon spin rotation/relaxation experiments combined with first-principles DFT calculations.
result: Characterization of muon (hydrogen) states in CeO2, including paramagnetic and diamagnetic fractions.
conclusion: The study provides insights into hydrogen incorporation in ceria but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Phase Transition And Negative Thermal Expansion In Copper Pyrophosphate ${\mathrm{Cu}}_{2}{\mathrm{P}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$ Studied By Neutron Total Scattering And The Reverse Monte Carlo Method
authors: Martin T. Dove, Naike Shi, Shaojie Wang, Jiaxin Song, Juping Xu, Wen Yin, Jun Chen, Yang Hai, And Guanqun Cai
abstract:
Author(s): Martin T. Dove, Naike Shi, Shaojie Wang, Jiaxin Song, Juping Xu, Wen Yin, Jun Chen, Yang Hai, and Guanqun Cai

The phase transition in copper pyrophosphate, [MATH], has been studied using neutron total scattering and the reverse Monte Carlo method. The results show the growth of disorder of the orientations of the [MATH] tetrahedra and of the position…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024309] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a structural phase transition and negative thermal expansion in copper pyrophosphate using neutron scattering and reverse Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanism of negative thermal expansion in copper pyrophosphate, which is a material science problem.
method: Neutron total scattering experiments combined with reverse Monte Carlo modeling to analyze atomic disorder and thermal expansion.
result: The phase transition involves orientational disorder of P2O7 tetrahedra and positional disorder of copper ions, leading to negative thermal expansion.
conclusion: The study provides a detailed structural explanation for the negative thermal expansion in this material.

title: Microscopic Origin Of Polarization-controlled Magnetization Switching In ${\mathrm{FePt}/\mathrm{BaTiO}}_{3}$
authors: Qurat Ul Ain, Thi H. Ho, Soon Cheol Hong, Dorj Odkhuu, And S. H. Rhim
abstract:
Author(s): Qurat ul ain, Thi H. Ho, Soon Cheol Hong, Dorj Odkhuu, and S. H. Rhim

Electric-field driven magnetization switching in [MATH] (001) is demonstrated through first-principles calculations. The magnetic easy axis of the FePt layer undergoes a transition from an in-plane to perpendicular direction upon ferroelectric polarization switching, a …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024414] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field-driven magnetization switching in FePt/BaTiO3 using first-principles calculations.
motivation: To understand the microscopic mechanism of polarization-controlled magnetization switching in multiferroic heterostructures.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations are performed on FePt/BaTiO3 (001) to compute magnetic anisotropy and electronic structure.
result: The magnetic easy axis of FePt switches from in-plane to perpendicular upon ferroelectric polarization reversal of BaTiO3.
conclusion: The study reveals a microscopic origin for magnetoelectric coupling in this system, which could be useful for spintronic devices.

title: Limited Propagation Of Pb-Pb Interactions Through Graphene And Pb Film Growth For Pb/graphene/Pb/SiC Intercalation Systems
authors: Yong Han, Shen Chen, Marek Kolmer, Michael C. Tringides, And James W. Evans
abstract:
Author(s): Yong Han, Shen Chen, Marek Kolmer, Michael C. Tringides, and James W. Evans

The growth of epitaxial thin films is directed by the substrate. Here, the authors investigate Pb film growth on SiC-supported graphene with an intercalated Pb(111)-like layer under graphene. They find that Pb–Pb interactions propagate only weakly through graphene, and that the potential energy surface for Pb adatoms does not inherit the periodicity of the intercalated Pb layer. Thus, the intercalated Pb(111) does not “remotely” direct the formation of a Pb(111) film. Nevertheless, the intercalated and on-top Pb(111)-like layers are in-registry reflecting their interaction with the same graphene sheet.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045417] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Pb film growth on graphene with an intercalated Pb layer, focusing on the limited propagation of Pb-Pb interactions through graphene.
motivation: Understanding how intercalated layers influence subsequent film growth is important for epitaxial thin film technology.
method: The authors investigate Pb film growth on SiC-supported graphene with an intercalated Pb(111)-like layer using experimental and theoretical methods.
result: Pb-Pb interactions propagate only weakly through graphene, and the potential energy surface for Pb adatoms does not inherit the periodicity of the intercalated Pb layer.
conclusion: The intercalated Pb(111) does not remotely direct the formation of a Pb(111) film, but the intercalated and on-top layers are in-registry due to interaction with the same graphene sheet.

title: Extremely Anisotropic Second Harmonic Generation In In-plane Janus Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Heterostructures
authors: Xiaozhendong Bao, Shi-Qi Li, Hu Chen, Qianyu Chen, Yifan Wu, Lichuan Zhang, Yuee Xie, And Yuanping Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaozhendong Bao, Shi-Qi Li, Hu Chen, Qianyu Chen, Yifan Wu, Lichuan Zhang, Yuee Xie, and Yuanping Chen

Anisotropic second harmonic generation (SHG) is of central importance in nonlinear photonics because it enables highly directional light manipulation and advanced polarization-sensitive functionalities. Here, taking two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides as a prototypical platform, we…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045418] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anisotropic second harmonic generation in Janus transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures, a topic in nonlinear photonics and materials science.
motivation: Anisotropic SHG enables directional light manipulation and polarization-sensitive functionalities, important for nonlinear photonics.
method: First-principles calculations are used to investigate the SHG properties of in-plane Janus TMD heterostructures.
result: Extremely anisotropic SHG is predicted in these heterostructures, with strong dependence on polarization and structure.
conclusion: Janus TMD heterostructures are promising platforms for anisotropic nonlinear optical devices.

title: Successive Semiconductor-metal-insulator Transition In The Mixed-valent Oxide $\mathrm{CaF}{\mathrm{e}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{5}$
authors: Hao-Hang Xu, Jian Liu, L. L. Tao, Xian-Jie Wang, Yu Sui, Ziyi Liu, And Jinguang Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Hang Xu, Jian Liu, L. L. Tao, Xian-Jie Wang, Yu Sui, Ziyi Liu, and Jinguang Cheng

A High-quality single crystal of [MATH] was grown using the floating-zone method, enabling a precise investigation of its electronic phase transitions. Temperature-dependent resistivity measurements reveal two successive semiconductor-metal-insulator transitio…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065116] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports successive semiconductor-metal-insulator transitions in a mixed-valent oxide CaFe3O5, focusing on electronic phase transitions in a condensed matter system.
motivation: To understand the electronic phase transitions in mixed-valent oxides, which are of interest in condensed matter physics but not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: High-quality single crystals were grown using the floating-zone method, and temperature-dependent resistivity measurements were performed to characterize the transitions.
result: Two successive semiconductor-metal-insulator transitions were observed, revealing complex electronic behavior.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the electronic properties of CaFe3O5, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ring Solitons And Lump Waves Of The Elliptic Cylindrical Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Equation In Physical Coordinates
authors: Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang, And Xiangyu Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang, and Xiangyu Yang

The elliptic cylindrical Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (ecKP) equation is derived from the incompressible Euler equations governing surface gravity waves with nearly elliptic fronts. Using Hirota's bilinear method, this paper systematically investigates ring solitons, lump chains, and lump waves of the ecK…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014216] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ring solitons and lump waves of the elliptic cylindrical Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation, which is a model for surface gravity waves with nearly elliptic fronts.
motivation: To understand nonlinear wave phenomena in fluid dynamics, specifically ring solitons and lump waves in elliptic cylindrical coordinates.
method: Uses Hirota's bilinear method to derive exact solutions of the ecKP equation.
result: Obtains ring solitons, lump chains, and lump waves in physical coordinates.
conclusion: The ecKP equation supports various nonlinear wave structures that may be relevant to fluid dynamics.

title: Filtered Rayleigh-Ritz And The Prony-Ritz Equivalence Class
authors: Ryan Abbott, Daniel C. Hackett, George T. Fleming, Dimitra A. Pefkou, And Michael L. Wagman
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Abbott, Daniel C. Hackett, George T. Fleming, Dimitra A. Pefkou, and Michael L. Wagman

Recent work [ 112, 054506 (2025);
tldr: This paper presents a method for extracting energy spectra from correlation functions in lattice quantum field theory using a filtered Rayleigh-Ritz approach and establishes an equivalence class with Prony-like methods.
motivation: Extracting excited-state energies and matrix elements from correlation functions is a fundamental challenge in lattice QCD and other quantum field theories.
method: The authors develop a filtered Rayleigh-Ritz method that uses a filter function to isolate eigenstates, and show its equivalence to the Prony method, leading to a unified framework.
result: The method provides a systematic way to extract multiple energy levels and matrix elements with controlled uncertainties, and the equivalence class clarifies the relationship between different extraction techniques.
conclusion: The filtered Rayleigh-Ritz method and its equivalence to Prony methods offer a robust tool for spectroscopy in lattice field theory, with potential applications beyond QCD.

title: Transmutation-accelerated Sampling Method For Multicomponent ZrCu(Al) Metallic Glasses
authors: Filip Kaśkosz, Rene Alvarez-Donado, Mikko Alava, Anshul D. S. Parmar, And Silvia Bonfanti
abstract:
Author(s): Filip Kaśkosz, Rene Alvarez-Donado, Mikko Alava, Anshul D. S. Parmar, and Silvia Bonfanti

We investigate multicomponent metallic glass systems using a hybrid molecular dynamics (MD) and variance-constrained semi-grand-canonical approach. This method enables us to generate samples with properties consistent with experimental observations, at deeply supercooled states that are typically in…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014117] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a hybrid molecular dynamics and variance-constrained semi-grand-canonical approach to simulate multicomponent metallic glasses.
motivation: To generate realistic samples of multicomponent metallic glasses at deeply supercooled states that match experimental observations.
method: Combines molecular dynamics with a variance-constrained semi-grand-canonical ensemble to accelerate sampling.
result: The method produces samples with properties consistent with experiments.
conclusion: The transmutation-accelerated sampling method is effective for studying multicomponent metallic glasses.

title: Multiphoton Ionization With Three-dimensional Light Fields
authors: D. Köhnke, H.-C. Ahlswede, T. Bayer, And M. Wollenhaupt
abstract:
Author(s): D. Köhnke, H.-C. Ahlswede, T. Bayer, and M. Wollenhaupt

We employ, for the first time, bichromatic three-dimensional (3D) polarization-shaped ultrashort laser fields in atomic multiphoton ionization to create previously inaccessible free-electron angular momentum wave packets. The 3D fields are created by the noncollinear superposition of two polarizatio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033048] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the use of bichromatic three-dimensional polarization-shaped laser fields to create free-electron angular momentum wave packets in atomic multiphoton ionization.
motivation: To explore the generation of previously inaccessible free-electron angular momentum wave packets using tailored light fields.
method: Noncollinear superposition of two polarization-shaped ultrashort laser pulses to create three-dimensional fields, applied to atomic multiphoton ionization.
result: Observation of free-electron angular momentum wave packets, demonstrating control over electron dynamics.
conclusion: Three-dimensional light fields enable new capabilities in controlling electron wave packets, with potential applications in ultrafast science.

title: Physics-informed Neural Networks For Solving Saddle-point Equations In Strong-field Physics With Tailored Fields
authors: Jiakang Chen, Sufia Hashim, And Carla Figueira de Morisson Faria
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakang Chen, Sufia Hashim, and Carla Figueira de Morisson Faria

We develop an unsupervised physics-informed neural network (PINN) to solve the saddle-point equations (SPEs) governing direct above-threshold ionization (ATI) within the strong-field approximation. This setting provides a well-understood test bed in which the saddle-point structure is known for tail…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033029] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses physics-informed neural networks to solve saddle-point equations in strong-field physics, specifically for above-threshold ionization.
motivation: Solving saddle-point equations in strong-field physics is computationally challenging; the authors aim to develop a machine learning approach that is efficient and accurate.
method: An unsupervised physics-informed neural network (PINN) is designed to solve the saddle-point equations governing direct above-threshold ionization within the strong-field approximation.
result: The PINN successfully reproduces known saddle-point structures and provides accurate solutions for tailored fields.
conclusion: Physics-informed neural networks offer a viable alternative for solving saddle-point equations in strong-field physics, with potential for extension to more complex scenarios.

title: Surface Phase Separation In A Confined Space
authors: Daoning Wu And Jie Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Daoning Wu and Jie Lin

Biomolecular condensates frequently form near surfaces, including lipid membranes. However, the effect of a surface on phase separation within a cell, a confined system, remains elusive. In this work, we study surface phase separation under the constraint of a finite number of molecules in a confine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033007] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies surface phase separation in confined spaces, relevant to biophysics and soft matter, but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates often form near surfaces, but the effect of confinement on phase separation is not well understood.
method: The authors theoretically model surface phase separation under finite molecule number constraints in a confined geometry.
result: They find that confinement alters phase behavior, leading to surface-induced phase separation with distinct scaling laws.
conclusion: Surface phase separation in confined spaces is a distinct phenomenon that may be relevant to cellular organization.

title: Shear Jamming Transition In Alternating Shear Rotation For Frictional And Frictionless Suspensions
authors: Pappu Acharya And Martin Trulsson
abstract:
Author(s): Pappu Acharya and Martin Trulsson

Alternating shear rotations in dense suspensions have recently shown the ability to reduce both viscosity and dissipation per strain (at a fixed global shear rate). Here, we study alternating shear rotations, with extensive numerical simulations, at various angles and up to their corresponding jammi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033013] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shear jamming transitions in dense suspensions under alternating shear rotations, focusing on rheological properties.
motivation: Understanding jamming transitions in suspensions is important for material processing, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Extensive numerical simulations of frictional and frictionless suspensions under alternating shear rotations at various angles.
result: Alternating shear rotations can reduce viscosity and dissipation per strain, and the jamming transition depends on the rotation angle.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into shear jamming but are purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi
